SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ: APP) faces a securities class action seeking to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired AppLovin securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026.
The suit follows the publication of a concerning analyst report on July 13, 2026 and the company's August 5, 2026 Q2 2026 financial results, each of which drove the price of AppLovin shares sharply lower.
The developments have prompted national shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman to open an investigation into claims that AppLovin violated the securities laws and urge AppLovin investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now.
Class Period: Feb. 12, 2026 – Aug. 5, 2026
AppLovin Corporation (APP) Securities Class Action:
AppLovin provides end-to-end AI-powered advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize, and grow their global audience.
To investors, "uplift" is possibly the most critical driver of the company's revenue growth. The company improves its AI model to increase uplift, better matching the exact right ad to the exact right user at the exact right millisecond. In turn, this uplifts advertisers' return on ad spend, increases their advertising budgets, and (for AppLovin) accelerates high-margin revenue.
The lawsuit is focused on the propriety of AppLovin's statements about model improvements and uplift.
Most recently, several weeks into AppLovin's Q2, during its May 6, 2026 Q1 2026 earnings call, management left investors with high expectations for uplift and revenue growth.
CEO Adam Foroughi said that the most important milestone investors should focus on was the company's "improving the underlying model." He emphasized that "[l]ast quarter earnings, I mentioned we just had one new model that had just created an uplift[]" and "[t]he one we had a couple of weeks ago was quite substantial." He also explained, "that's why I highlighted […] that we saw a big acceleration going exiting the quarter[,]" and "then, April Q2, bigger than any quarter that we had[.]"
Investors' expectations began to unravel on July 13, 2026, when a prominent analyst published a report highlighting a lack of immediate advertiser influx following the general availability launch of AppLovin's advertising tools. In response, the price of AppLovin shares tumbled $64.13 (-12.6%).
Then, on August 5, 2026, the company reported its Q2 2026 revenue that was below midpoint. In apparent contrast to the "big acceleration," management said "[o]ur pace of meaningful model improvement was lighter than normal during the quarter[]" and "we didn't get the same level of model uplift we've seen in recent quarters[.]" This news drove the price of AppLovin shares crashing another $82.13 (-19.6%).
Between the two drops, the company lost over $44 billion of its market capitalization.
"We're focused on when during Q2 AppLovin first knew that the uplift and revenue acceleration investors had come to expect wasn't happening," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.
If you invested in AppLovin and have substantial losses, or have knowledge that will assist the firm's investigation, submit your losses now »
Whistleblowers: Persons with non-public information regarding AppLovin should consider their options to help in the investigation or take advantage of the SEC Whistleblower program. Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. For more information, call Reed Kathrein at 844-916-0895 or email [email protected].

How Quarterly Results Will Impact AppLovin Stock Investors
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 3:12 PM CDT 5 min read
AppLovin recently opened its Ads Manager platform to public self-serve access, while guiding for high adjusted EBITDA margins and acknowledging a slower revenue trajectory and an execution miss against earlier expectations.
The AI powered ad engine that drives almost all of AppLovin's sales is now both the growth lever and the primary operational risk, as management works to improve models without letting compute and legal costs erode profitability.
The focus now turns to how this earnings reset, particularly the downward estimate revisions, reshapes AppLovin's investment narrative and risk balance.

To own AppLovin, you need to believe its AI ad engine can keep delivering strong results for advertisers while the firm broadens beyond gaming into consumer and mid market clients. The recent reset in growth expectations and margin guidance puts the spotlight on execution quality rather than long term ambition. In the near term, the main upside catalyst remains clear model improvements that support ad spend without inflating compute costs.
The biggest near term risk is that slowing revenue momentum, legal overhangs around AI disclosures and data access, and heavier privacy demands combine to pressure profitability. Q3 results in early November are an important check on whether the recent Ads Manager upgrade and model refresh are translating into healthier advertiser budgets and stable cash generation.
The opening of AppLovin's Ads Manager to public self serve access is the most relevant development for this reset. You now have a business that is trying to turn a historically high touch, gaming led engine into a broader, more automated platform that mid market and consumer advertisers can use directly. That decision makes the growth story less about a few large accounts and more about onboarding, retention and model accuracy at scale.
This expansion path also sharpens both the upside and the risk around AXON model upgrades. Better tooling and easier onboarding can support catalysts such as diversification into consumer, lead generation and connected TV through Wurl. At the same time, any misstep that increases compute, compliance or legal expense faster than new budgets arrive, especially with the stock already down more than 50% over the past year, would weigh heavily on how investors view execution quality.
What The Current AppLovin Forecasts Assume
Analysts sketch a fairly specific picture of where AppLovin could land by the end of this decade. The current consensus points to earnings today of about US$4.4b and forecast consensus earnings of US$8.5b by 2029, which implies roughly a doubling of profit. The same group is baking in forecast revenue growth of 24.4% per year over the next three years and a forecast revenue level of about US$13.1b by that 2029 estimate year. In simple terms, the earnings change required is an increase of roughly US$4.1b, taking AppLovin from US$4.4b to US$8.5b on the timeline analysts are using.

NEW YORK, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leading securities law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) and certain of the company's senior executives for securities fraud after significant stock drops resulting from potential violations of the federal securities laws.
If you invested in AppLovin, you are encouraged to obtain additional information by visiting: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/applovin-class-action-lawsuit.
Key Details of the AppLovin ($APP) Class Action:
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: November 16, 2026
Alleged Misconduct: Securities fraud alleging AppLovin misrepresented the strength, viability, and development of its AI-based business model and products
Largest Alleged Stock Drop: August 5, 2026 – 20% Stock Drop
Court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
Action: Contact BFA Law to discuss your rights
Investors have until November 16, 2026 to ask the Court to be appointed to lead the case. The complaint asserts securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of investors in AppLovin securities. The class action is pending in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. It is captioned Talbot v. AppLovin Corp., et al., No. 26-cv-10584.
Why is AppLovin Being Sued for Securities Fraud?
AppLovin is an advertising solutions company. AppLovin claims its advertising products use artificial intelligence ("AI") models, among other things, to more effectively match advertisers to prospective customers.
According to the complaint, AppLovin touted the purported strength of the company's AI models as a major driver of the company's growth, telling investors that AppLovin was "constantly improving" its models and that "we don't really see a reason why that's going to slow down."
As alleged, the company's new generative AI video tool in its AppLovin Ads platform experienced significant development delays, which stymied improvements to AppLovin's AI model.
Why did AppLovin's Stock Drop?
On July 13, 2026, a Bank of America Securities analyst published a note stating that "AppLovin's eCommerce footprint expanded at a slower pace in June" and "[w]eekly data has not shown a clear uptick since AppLovin [Ads] opened to all eComm advertisers on 6/22, suggesting a muted GA start." Accordingly, Bank of America Securities lowered its estimate for AppLovin's annual revenue.
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $64.13 per share, or 12.6%, from a closing price of $506.80 per share on July 10, 2026, to a closing price of $442.85 per share on July 13, 2026.
Then, on August 5, 2026, after the market closed, AppLovin announced that it missed consensus estimates for quarterly revenue, delivering $1.92 billion of revenue against consensus estimates of $1.94 billion. Defendants attributed the miss, in part, to delays in the roll out of AppLovin Ads' generative AI video creation tool, which led to lower-than-expected AppLovin Ads revenue and hampered AppLovin's AI "model performance[.]"
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $82.13 per share, or 19.6%, from a closing price of $417.80 per share on August 5, 2026, to a closing price of $335.67 per share on August 6, 2026.

AppLovin Corporation (APP) Grew Revenue 53%. What Must Happen to Defend Its Valuation?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:32 AM CDT 5 min read
AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) reported second-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 53%, yet its stock fell sharply after missing revenue expectations and management's own execution standard. The tension is not whether the advertising platform is growing; it is whether machine-learning improvements can sustain the exceptional margins and earnings trajectory implied by its valuation. In early October, analysts began questioning competing ad platforms' progress and the reliability of new e-commerce adoption signals. This makes AppLovin's stock less a straightforward growth story than a test of how durable its targeting advantage really is.
Second-quarter revenue reached $1.92 billion against a $1.94 billion consensus estimate, while EPS of $3.76 matched expectations. Adjusted EBITDA increased 58% to $1.61 billion, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin above 80%. Management said its important advertising-model upgrade arrived just after the quarter closed. The problem was timing rather than a reported collapse in customer demand, according to management, but the distinction matters only if later results confirm it.
AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) ranks fourth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit, behind three companies with very different economics. The more interesting comparison is whether AppLovin's extraordinary operating profitability can survive a market in which rivals increasingly adopt similar AI tools.
Zeta Global (ZETA) Tumbles as AI Dreams Turn to Nightmares
Incremental Compute Spending Could Help or Hurt
The company's advertising auctions improve as its models become more effective at predicting which ads produce sales. When advertisers earn better returns, they may expand budgets, giving AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) more data and incremental revenue. The company guided Q3 revenue to $2.055 billion to $2.085 billion, up 46% to 48% year-over-year, alongside $1.71 billion to $1.74 billion of adjusted EBITDA and an approximately 83% margin. That guidance assumes model improvements already deployed, not hypothetical later releases.
Yet compute is not free. Management explained that higher training costs are being undertaken where incremental returns justify them. It said roughly ten cents of each incremental revenue dollar could be spent on compute. An 80%-plus adjusted EBITDA margin gives the company considerable room for investment, but also means small efficiency setbacks can have an outsized impact on investor assumptions about its operating leverage.
The expansion beyond games has its own measurement problem; how AppLovin is extending its AI platform into e-commerce advertising analyzes why a larger addressable market does not immediately translate into verified revenue. Competition is another pressure point. In October, a court declined AppLovin's request for interim relief concerning Unity's Ad Quality SDK, without ruling on the underlying allegations. Jefferies' survey of mobile-game ad buyers led it to raise estimates for Unity while lowering its 2027 AppLovin revenue forecast by 5% and EBITDA estimate by 7%.
The Discount Is Real, but So Is the Premium
The Seeking Alpha data places AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) at 20.16 times trailing GAAP earnings and 16.76 times forward GAAP earnings, with forward non-GAAP P/E of 15.81. That last measure sits roughly 46% below the company's five-year average of 29.17, but about 26% above the sector median of 12.52. Forward enterprise value to sales is 10.91, nearly six times the sector median of 1.88. Accordingly, a much lower earnings multiple relative to AppLovin's history does not mean the business is inexpensive on every basis.
The consensus expects EPS growth of 60.49% in 2026, 27.30% in 2027, and 24.88% in 2028. The estimated P/E correspondingly falls from 16.76 on 2026 earnings to 13.16 on 2027 earnings and 10.54 on 2028 earnings, assuming a constant stock price and forecast delivery. The steepest growth is front-loaded, so valuation depends heavily on the bridge from rapid model-led gains to a more sustainable rate.
Free cash flow reached $863 million in Q2. Management expects full-year free cash flow conversion to normalize near 75% of adjusted EBITDA after tax and interest timing effects. The company ended the period with $3.05 billion in cash and around $3.7 billion in debt and repurchased or withheld about $551 million of stock. These are meaningful financial supports, but do not settle the question of how much customer acquisition efficiency can improve from today's elevated level.
Institutional Conviction Faces a Near-Term Test
Q2 2026 hedge fund ownership declined to 88 from 91 funds, while short positions increased to 11.61 million shares on September 30 from 10.56 million a month earlier, equaling 3.99% of float. The positioning is not exceptionally bearish by itself, but the direction contrasts with continued strong revenue growth.
Price-target cuts further illustrate the gap between current profitability and confidence in its future trajectory. On October 12, Oppenheimer reduced its target to $490 from $560 while lowering its FY2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA forecasts; BofA maintained Neutral but reduced its target to $325 from $400 on October 9, arguing that a durable reacceleration would be needed to justify a premium to other advertising giants. Wedbush remained Outperform at $560 from $610 on October 14 but reset estimates to a more achievable baseline.
The immediate test is therefore not simply another 50% revenue-growth quarter. It is whether the Q3 model upgrade drives measurable ad spending, consumer-advertising diversification, and cash conversion without permanently higher compute intensity. A different Reddit screen asks which stocks investors expect to rise dramatically despite substantial uncertainty, underscoring the distinction between an exciting growth narrative and the earnings needed to support its price.
While we acknowledge the potential of APP as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. AppLovin (APP) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.
Shares of this mobile app technology company have returned -13.6% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +1.5% change. The Zacks Technology Services industry, to which AppLovin belongs, has lost 8.1% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?
Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.
Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.
Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, AppLovin is expected to post earnings of $3.95 per share, indicating a change of +61.2% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.2% over the last 30 days.
For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $15.67 points to a change of +56.1% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has changed -0.3%.
For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $19.9 indicates a change of +27% from what AppLovin is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -1.3%.
Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, AppLovin is rated Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).
The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:
Even though a company's earnings growth is arguably the best indicator of its financial health, nothing much happens if it cannot raise its revenues. It's almost impossible for a company to grow its earnings without growing its revenue for long periods. Therefore, knowing a company's potential revenue growth is crucial.
In the case of AppLovin, the consensus sales estimate of $2.08 billion for the current quarter points to a year-over-year change of +47.8%. The $8.08 billion and $10.14 billion estimates for the current and next fiscal years indicate changes of +39.1% and +25.5%, respectively.
Last Reported Results and Surprise History
AppLovin reported revenues of $1.92 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +52.8%. EPS of $3.76 for the same period compares with $2.26 a year ago.
Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.94 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of -0.75%. The EPS surprise was +1.08%.
The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates three times over this period.
Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.
While comparing the current values of a company's valuation multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), with its own historical values helps determine whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of the reasonability of the stock's price.
As part of the Zacks Style Scores system, the Zacks Value Style Score (which evaluates both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics) organizes stocks into five groups ranging from A to F (A is better than B; B is better than C; and so on), making it helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.
AppLovin is graded C on this front, indicating that it is trading at par with its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.

Why Is AppLovin a Good Business?
Sitting at the crossroads of the mobile advertising ecosystem with over 200 free-to-play games in its portfolio, AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) provides software solutions that help mobile app developers market, monetize, and grow their apps through AI-powered advertising and analytics tools.
1. Long-Term Revenue Growth Shows Strong Momentum
Examining a company's long-term performance can provide clues about its quality. Even a bad business can shine for one or two quarters, but a top-tier one grows for years. Luckily, AppLovin's sales grew at a solid 25.8% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years. Its growth surpassed the average software company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.
2. Customer Acquisition Costs Are Recovered in Record Time
The customer acquisition cost (CAC) payback period represents the months required to recover the cost of acquiring a new customer. Essentially, it's the break-even point for sales and marketing investments. A shorter CAC payback period is ideal, as it implies better returns on investment and business scalability.
AppLovin is extremely efficient at acquiring new customers, and its CAC payback period checked in at 1.3 months this quarter. The company's rapid recovery of its customer acquisition costs indicates it has a highly differentiated product offering and a strong brand reputation. These dynamics give AppLovin more resources to pursue new product initiatives while maintaining the flexibility to increase its sales and marketing investments.
3. Excellent Free Cash Flow Margin Boosts Reinvestment Potential
If you've followed StockStory for a while, you know we emphasize free cash flow. Why, you ask? We believe that in the end, cash is king, and you can't use accounting profits to pay the bills.
AppLovin has shown terrific cash profitability, driven by its lucrative business model and cost-effective customer acquisition strategy that enable it to stay ahead of the competition through investments in new products rather than sales and marketing. The company's free cash flow margin was among the best in the software sector, averaging an eye-popping 66.3% over the last year.

AppLovin Just Dropped 12% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:50 PM CDT 4 min read
AppLovin Just Dropped 12% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up? ©@Creativa Images via Canva; @peshkov from Getty Images via Canva
AppLovin stock fell 12.6% in the month through October 19, as advertising-growth concerns, litigation, and analyst price-target cuts weighed on investor sentiment.
Seven investment firms reduced their price targets between October 8 and October 19, although five maintained Buy-equivalent ratings.
APP recently traded at around 14x forward earnings, significantly below its five-year average, while consensus estimates still suggest substantial earnings growth.
The November 4 earnings report could determine whether AppLovin's valuation discount presents a buying opportunity or reflects deeper business challenges.
AppLovin (APP:NASDAQ) stock fell 12.6% in the month through October 19, compared with a 0.6% gain for the S&P 500.
Concerns about AI-model improvements, litigation, and analyst target reductions have weighed on sentiment.
Yet earnings expectations have held up considerably better than the stock price, raising an important question: Has the market already priced in too much bad news?
What's Driving AppLovin Stock Lower?
AppLovin reported second-quarter revenue of $1.924 billion, up 53% year over year but slightly below analysts' expectations of $1.94 billion.
CEO Adam Foroughi acknowledged weaker-than-usual improvements in the company's AI-driven advertising models during the quarter.
Meanwhile, AppLovin faced securities class-action allegations involving its AI technology and an ongoing legal dispute with Unity Software (U:NYSE).
For comparison, Unity reported second-quarter revenue of $546 million, up 24% year over year. AppLovin's 53% revenue growth was considerably faster, although the companies' business mixes differ.
That growth advantage matters, but investors are increasingly concerned about whether AppLovin can sustain its momentum.
Wall Street Is Cutting AppLovin's Price Targets
Seven major investment firms reduced their AppLovin price targets between October 8 and October 19.
Jefferies lowered its target from $550 to $375, while Citi reduced its target from $600 to $500.
However, five maintained Buy-equivalent ratings, suggesting analysts remain cautiously optimistic despite near-term uncertainty.
AppLovin (APP): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
According to TIKR data, AppLovin's average analyst price target declined from approximately $744 in January to around $477.
The consensus target nevertheless remained substantially above the October 19 closing price of $269.12, suggesting Wall Street still sees meaningful potential upside.
AppLovin's Earnings Outlook Remains Strong
Despite the selloff, analysts have not reduced earnings expectations nearly as aggressively.
TIKR consensus estimates project normalized earnings per share rising from $10.64 in 2025 to approximately $21 by 2027, representing nearly 93% cumulative growth.
AppLovin (APP): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024–2029 (TIKR)
The contrast suggests that valuation compression, rather than collapsing earnings expectations, has driven much of the decline.
AppLovin (APP): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)
On October 16, APP traded at 14.3x forward earnings, compared with its five-year average of 25.6x.
That represents approximately 56% of its historical average valuation.
However, a lower multiple does not automatically mean a stock is undervalued, particularly if future earnings expectations decline.
Is AppLovin Stock a Buy or Sell After Its 12% Drop?
AppLovin looks more like a cautious buying opportunity than a stock investors need to sell simply because of its recent decline.
The company continues to generate strong revenue growth, while its valuation has contracted significantly.
AppLovin expects third-quarter revenue between $2.055 billion and $2.085 billion, with adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.710 billion to $1.740 billion.
AppLovin will report third-quarter results on November 4, after the market closes.
If AppLovin meets guidance and demonstrates renewed AI-model improvements, its discounted valuation could offer substantial long-term upside.
However, another disappointing quarter could trigger further earnings-estimate reductions and share-price pressure.
For patient investors, APP presents a potential buying opportunity rather than an obvious sell, but the November earnings report will be critical in determining whether the selloff has gone too far.

How Did Seagate (STX) Triple Selling a Technology Everyone Buried?
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 9:32 AM CDT 3 min read
Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ:STX) closed at $690.81 on October 15. The stock returned 29.90% over the last 6 months, compared with a 15.4% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 11.4% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.
Hard disk drives store data on spinning magnetic platters. They have been declared obsolete for most of two decades, steadily replaced in laptops and phones by flash memory with no moving parts. Seagate is one of only three companies that still makes them at scale. Its shares are up 206.48% over the past year, which is not how the story of a dying technology usually goes.
READ ALSO: 10 Most Undervalued Quality Stocks to Invest In
How Did Seagate (STX) Triple Selling a Technology Everyone Buried?
The Part Nobody Priced In:
Flash replaced hard drives where speed matters and size does not. It never replaced them where the opposite is true, which is storing enormous quantities of data that is rarely read.
Artificial intelligence produced exactly that kind of data, in volumes nobody had planned storage for. Hard drives remain considerably cheaper per unit of capacity, and at the scale data centres now operate, that difference decides the purchase.
The financial effect has been dramatic. Revenue rose 48.5% in the most recent quarter, and earnings grew 165.2%. Seagate holds one of the widest analyst gaps in our 10 Most Promising Technology Stocks to Buy Right Now. To see the rest, click HERE.
Three Companies and a Long Memory:
The pricing power comes from scarcity of supply rather than from anything special about the product. Three firms make these drives, and Seagate has told investors that the capacity it sells to data centres is fully allocated through this year. Demand arrived faster than the industry could serve it.
That is a condition rather than an advantage. Any competitor adding output changes it, and the industry has a long history of prices falling once supply catches up with demand. The balance sheet carries its own tension. Debt runs at 179.88% of equity, which is manageable while cash is flooding in and considerably less so if the pricing that produced it goes away.
DON'T MISS: 10 Best Stocks to Buy for High Returns in 2026
A Cyclical Business at a Cyclical Price:
The shares change hands at 25.71 times what analysts expect next year, against 66.17 times the past year. The forward figure is the one the market is actually using, and it still assumes earnings stay far above where this business used to operate.
Everything rests on the shortage lasting. Judge that wrong and 25.71 times peak earnings turns into a far larger number on normal ones, which is the arithmetic that has caught buyers of this industry before.
Conclusion:
The technology was never finished, only pushed into the corner of the market where cost per unit of capacity beats speed. That corner then became the fastest-growing part of storage, which nobody forecast. The rise is real, and the reason for it is sound, but it rests on three companies having too little capacity rather than on anything a competitor cannot copy. Watch what any of them announces about building more, because that is the thing that ends this.

That growth lifted shares 174.44% this year and carried them to a 52-week high of $1,143.27. The stock now sits about 34% below that peak after Barron’s flagged a Toshiba problem for hard drive makers.
Sold-Out Capacity and Rising Estimates Power the Bull Case
Seagate’s forward earnings multiple is 26, while its trailing multiple is 56, a gap that shows how fast profits are growing. The fiscal 2027 EPS consensus is $36.2661, up from $27.7398 90 days ago. Analysts made zero downward revisions over the past 30 days.
Management said nearline capacity is almost fully allocated through calendar 2027, and pricing on fiscal 2027 contracts is already set. Seagate has beaten EPS estimates five straight quarters. Last quarter it posted $5.71 against a $5.0932 consensus, and it guided fiscal Q1 EPS to $7.30.
Cyclical Scars and a Beta Above 2 Keep Bears Circling
Hard drive demand has always moved in cycles. In fiscal 2023, Seagate lost $529 million. Data center sales now make up 80% of revenue, and that business leans on a few of hyperscalers whose spending could slow quickly.
Shares trade at 14.6 times sales and carry a beta of 2.081. Toshiba, Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC), and flash storage all compete for the same customers, and exchangeable notes due 2028 could dilute shareholders. One analyst rates the stock a Strong Sell.
Mozaic 4 Ramp Will Decide Whether Patience Pays
The stock fell 9.19% over the past month and trades below its 50-day moving average of $855.24. It still holds above its 200-day average of $663.81.
Execution will decide the next move. Mozaic 4 should cross over with Mozaic 3 toward the end of calendar 2026, and HAMR drives take longer to produce than the older technology. Fiscal Q1 results against $4.10 billion revenue guidance will tip the scale. A miss would favor sellers. A beat coupled with stronger fiscal 2027 commentary would favor buyers.

Seagate trades at $753.25, and the average analyst target is $1,142.17, meaning 51.6% upside. The 25 covering analysts rate the stock as follows:

Earnings Momentum Keeps Seagate’s AI Growth Story in Focus
At $753.25, Seagate trades well below the average analyst target.
Earnings are the path higher. Revenue grew 48.49% year over year last quarter, and GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.3% from 37.4%. Locked-in capacity means those gains rest on signed contracts.
The fiscal Q1 report is the next big catalyst. If Seagate meets its $7.30 EPS guide and confirms 2027 pricing, view could recover from the Toshiba shock. Over the next year, the shift to Mozaic 4 should push margins higher still.
Three things would break the thesis: hyperscaler order cuts, falling revenue per terabyte, or a HAMR yield setback. Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) Rides AI Storage Demand, Is It Still Undervalued?
Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) is back in focus as investors track rising demand for memory and storage tied to AI workloads, along with its HAMR-based Mozaic platform for higher-capacity, power-efficient drives.
Recent trading has been strong for Seagate Technology Holdings, with a 1-day share price return of 1.20% and a 30-day share price gain of 10.49% helping offset a 90-day share price decline of 4.99% as investors reassess AI storage demand and risk. For anyone looking beyond the latest move to US$916.83, the stock shows notable momentum in the background. The year-to-date share price return is 218.85% and the 1-year total shareholder return is 303.74%. These contribute to a very large 3-year and 5-year total shareholder return that both exceed 10x.
Scan beyond Seagate Technology Holdings and see which storage and AI infrastructure peers are also attracting attention in the 85 AI infrastructure stocks.
Seagate Technology Holdings now sits on a huge AI storage story and a share price that has already moved sharply. The real tension is whether that momentum still lines up with a sensible valuation.
Most Popular Narrative: 20.9% Undervalued
On the narrative view, Seagate Technology Holdings is priced at $916.83 against an implied fair value of $1,158.73, which suggests the share price sits below where the story says it should be while also running far ahead of where it started this year.
Seagate is the storage-capacity position in a portfolio built on physical scarcity, and it''s the one I''d defend furthest into a downturn.
Not because the shortage is more durable than the others, it may or may not be. Because Seagate is the only one of my three storage holdings with a margin lever that runs independently of the pricing cycle.
See why 6 investors see Seagate Technology Holdings as 21% undervalued.
The most followed storyline, according to isidrohg, rests on two moving parts that both matter for valuation. The first is a tight nearline HDD market where supply has not seen new capacity in roughly a decade. The second is the HAMR driven Mozaic platform, which is described as pushing areal density higher so that each exabyte shipped requires fewer physical components, lowering unit costs even if pricing conditions change.
In that framework, Seagate Technology Holdings is treated less like a simple pricing beneficiary and more like a business with its own internal cost curve. The narrative points to HAMR penetration moving from roughly 40% of nearline exabyte shipments toward a targeted 70% by June 2027, and links that shift directly to higher gross margins that are tied to technology mix rather than solely to contract prices.
Supporters of this view also highlight how that cost lever interacts with capital allocation and balance sheet choices. The emphasis on using recent free cash flow to cut debt, rather than pouring money into new greenfield capacity, is framed as a way to keep the current HDD duopoly tight, which in turn underpins the cash flow assumptions that feed into the fair value estimate of $1,158.73.
Result: Fair Value of $1,158.73 (UNDERVALUED)
Still, Seagate Technology Holdings faces two clear pressure points: a potential HDD duopoly crack from new capacity and Western Digital closing the HAMR efficiency gap faster than expected.
Find out about the key risks to this Seagate Technology Holdings narrative.
Another View: What Seagate's P/E Is Telling Investors
The narrative and cash flow work suggest Seagate Technology Holdings trades roughly 21% below a fair value of $1,158.73. A simple P/E cross-check tells a very different story. At 65.5x earnings, the stock is far richer than both peers on 25.8x and the wider Tech group on 19.8x, and it also sits above an estimated fair ratio of 54.8x. That kind of gap points to real valuation risk if the growth story slips even modestly. The key question is which lens you trust more when the next wobble hits.

How Did Seagate (STX) Triple Selling a Technology Everyone Buried?
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 9:32 AM CDT 3 min read
Seagate Technology Holdings plc (NASDAQ:STX) closed at $690.81 on October 15. The stock returned 29.90% over the last 6 months, compared with a 15.4% return for the Insider Monkey Billionaire Index and 11.4% for the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust.
Hard disk drives store data on spinning magnetic platters. They have been declared obsolete for most of two decades, steadily replaced in laptops and phones by flash memory with no moving parts. Seagate is one of only three companies that still makes them at scale. Its shares are up 206.48% over the past year, which is not how the story of a dying technology usually goes.
READ ALSO: 10 Most Undervalued Quality Stocks to Invest In
How Did Seagate (STX) Triple Selling a Technology Everyone Buried?
The Part Nobody Priced In:
Flash replaced hard drives where speed matters and size does not. It never replaced them where the opposite is true, which is storing enormous quantities of data that is rarely read.
Artificial intelligence produced exactly that kind of data, in volumes nobody had planned storage for. Hard drives remain considerably cheaper per unit of capacity, and at the scale data centres now operate, that difference decides the purchase.
The financial effect has been dramatic. Revenue rose 48.5% in the most recent quarter, and earnings grew 165.2%. Seagate holds one of the widest analyst gaps in our 10 Most Promising Technology Stocks to Buy Right Now. To see the rest, click HERE.
Three Companies and a Long Memory:
The pricing power comes from scarcity of supply rather than from anything special about the product. Three firms make these drives, and Seagate has told investors that the capacity it sells to data centres is fully allocated through this year. Demand arrived faster than the industry could serve it.
That is a condition rather than an advantage. Any competitor adding output changes it, and the industry has a long history of prices falling once supply catches up with demand. The balance sheet carries its own tension. Debt runs at 179.88% of equity, which is manageable while cash is flooding in and considerably less so if the pricing that produced it goes away.
DON'T MISS: 10 Best Stocks to Buy for High Returns in 2026
A Cyclical Business at a Cyclical Price:
The shares change hands at 25.71 times what analysts expect next year, against 66.17 times the past year. The forward figure is the one the market is actually using, and it still assumes earnings stay far above where this business used to operate.
Everything rests on the shortage lasting. Judge that wrong and 25.71 times peak earnings turns into a far larger number on normal ones, which is the arithmetic that has caught buyers of this industry before.
Conclusion:
The technology was never finished, only pushed into the corner of the market where cost per unit of capacity beats speed. That corner then became the fastest-growing part of storage, which nobody forecast. The rise is real, and the reason for it is sound, but it rests on three companies having too little capacity rather than on anything a competitor cannot copy. Watch what any of them announces about building more, because that is the thing that ends this.

Rapid Growth, High Volatility, and Near 50% Upside Confound Seagate Technology Investors
Seagate shares cratered 15% in a single week even as analysts refused to cut a single earnings estimate and the stock still sits nearly 52% below where the average price target says it should be. Something in that gap is…
Published October 13, 2026, 10:45am ET · 3 min read
A close-up of an "AI" chip on a circuit board illustrates the complex technology at the heart of the interpretability debate. © Quality Stock Arts / Shutterstock.com
Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX | STX Price Prediction) trades at $753.25 after a sharp decline left the AI storage leader trading far below analyst targets. Shares fell 15.09% in one week even as earnings estimates kept climbing.
Seagate is a leading supplier of mass-capacity hard drives for cloud data centers. Its Mozaic platform uses heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) to fit more data onto each disk. Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 34.06% to $12.195 billion, and free cash flow reached a record $3.1 billion.
That growth lifted shares 174.44% this year and carried them to a 52-week high of $1,143.27. The stock now sits about 34% below that peak after Barron’s flagged a Toshiba problem for hard drive makers.
Sold-Out Capacity and Rising Estimates Power the Bull Case
Seagate’s forward earnings multiple is 26, while its trailing multiple is 56, a gap that shows how fast profits are growing. The fiscal 2027 EPS consensus is $36.2661, up from $27.7398 90 days ago. Analysts made zero downward revisions over the past 30 days.
Management said nearline capacity is almost fully allocated through calendar 2027, and pricing on fiscal 2027 contracts is already set. Seagate has beaten EPS estimates five straight quarters. Last quarter it posted $5.71 against a $5.0932 consensus, and it guided fiscal Q1 EPS to $7.30.
Cyclical Scars and a Beta Above 2 Keep Bears Circling
Hard drive demand has always moved in cycles. In fiscal 2023, Seagate lost $529 million. Data center sales now make up 80% of revenue, and that business leans on a few of hyperscalers whose spending could slow quickly.
Shares trade at 14.6 times sales and carry a beta of 2.081. Toshiba, Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC), and flash storage all compete for the same customers, and exchangeable notes due 2028 could dilute shareholders. One analyst rates the stock a Strong Sell.
Mozaic 4 Ramp Will Decide Whether Patience Pays
The stock fell 9.19% over the past month and trades below its 50-day moving average of $855.24. It still holds above its 200-day average of $663.81.
Execution will decide the next move. Mozaic 4 should cross over with Mozaic 3 toward the end of calendar 2026, and HAMR drives take longer to produce than the older technology. Fiscal Q1 results against $4.10 billion revenue guidance will tip the scale. A miss would favor sellers. A beat coupled with stronger fiscal 2027 commentary would favor buyers.
Analysts See 51.6% Upside While Short-Term Momentum Lags
Seagate trades at $753.25, and the average analyst target is $1,142.17, meaning 51.6% upside. The 25 covering analysts rate the stock as follows:
Seagate is up 174.44% this year, while the S&P 500 is up 14.1%. Over one year the gap is 253.46% against 19.15%. The past week went the other way: Seagate dropped 15.09% while the index rose 0.42%. Price targets are estimates, and analysts can cut them as quickly as the stock falls.
Earnings Momentum Keeps Seagate’s AI Growth Story in Focus
At $753.25, Seagate trades well below the average analyst target.
Earnings are the path higher. Revenue grew 48.49% year over year last quarter, and GAAP gross margin expanded to 52.3% from 37.4%. Locked-in capacity means those gains rest on signed contracts.
The fiscal Q1 report is the next big catalyst. If Seagate meets its $7.30 EPS guide and confirms 2027 pricing, view could recover from the Toshiba shock. Over the next year, the shift to Mozaic 4 should push margins higher still.
Three things would break the thesis: hyperscaler order cuts, falling revenue per terabyte, or a HAMR yield setback. The same data-center expansion driving Seagate’s sold-out nearline capacity also powers a wider group of non-chip suppliers we profiled in a free report on seven AI infrastructure stocks that aren’t chipmakers. With a beta above 2, expect big moves in both directions along the way.
Analysts made no down estimate revisions during this double-digit weekly sell-off, a sign that analyst conviction in one of the market’s clearest AI storage stories held firm.

Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) could see its market valuation nearly double as relentless demand for data storage tightens global supplies, according to a recent research note from Morgan Stanley.
Morgan Stanley maintained their ‘overweight’ rating on the data storage giant while nudging their 12-month price target up to $1,200 from $1,187, an 82% upside potential compared to the stock's previous closing price.

"We remain convicted in hard disk drives earnings upside despite an elongated catalyst path," wrote Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring in a communication to clients. Supply Deficits And Accelerating Pricing
Market pressures have intensified as demand for hard disk drives (HDDs) thoroughly outpaces manufacturing output. According to industry figures cited from HSBC, the market currently faces a staggering 400-exabyte shortfall in HDD capacity.
Woodring compared the current trajectory of the hard disk drive sector to the memory market from the previous year, noting that profit margins remain well below their cyclical peaks. With pricing accelerating rapidly, a more consequential market inflection point remains on the horizon.
Recent spot market deals executed by Seagate reflect this tightness, with transactions pricing anywhere from two to five times higher than baseline contract levels, which is expected to provide further catalysts for stock appreciation.

Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) Eyes TDK HDD Head Deal As AI Storage Demand Builds
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 1:12 PM CDT 3 min read
Seagate Technology Holdings (NasdaqGS: STX) and Toshiba are in talks to acquire TDK's hard disk drive magnetic head business.
The potential transaction would transfer TDK's HDD magnetic head operations, a key component in high capacity storage devices, to the two buyers.
The discussions come as demand for AI data storage puts extra focus on securing core HDD technologies and supply chains.
The proposed purchase of TDK's HDD magnetic head unit by Seagate and Toshiba only captures one angle of today's story. Our analysis turns up 3 warning signs for Seagate Technology Holdings as well.
Rising interest in AI infrastructure makes it worth scanning a broader group of hardware and storage plays through 55 AI infrastructure stocks.
NasdaqGS:STX Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Oct 2026
Seagate Technology Holdings supplies data storage hardware and related solutions across the US, Singapore, the Netherlands, and other regions, so tighter control of HDD magnetic head technology would plug directly into how its products are designed and manufactured. The group already operates at scale, with a reported market value of about $162.3b. This scale can influence how counterparties approach complex asset deals like this one.
3 things going right for Seagate Technology Holdings that this headline doesn't cover.
What TDK's HDD heads could mean for Seagate's HAMR roadmap and pricing power
For Seagate Technology Holdings, potential access to TDK's HDD magnetic head unit ties directly into the Mozaic HAMR roadmap that underpins its Narrative. Control over a critical input for heat assisted magnetic recording aligns with the catalyst that hinges on Mozaic driven capacity per drive and margin mix, and it could support the long term build to order contracts that already allocate most nearline exabytes through 2028. At the same time, closer collaboration with Toshiba on heads interacts with the existing risk that extra HDD capacity may chip away at industry supply discipline and future pricing per exabyte.

From here, the key marker to watch is how Seagate quantifies HAMR adoption, particularly whether Mozaic products move from roughly 40% of nearline exabyte shipments toward the next disclosed milestone in calendar 2026, and how any TDK transaction is referenced in that progress update.
One more thing Seagate investors should look at before moving on

Investing.com -- Morgan Stanley on Tuesday lowered its price target on Western Digital to $643 from $676, while raising its target on Seagate Technology to $1,200 from $1,187, citing growing uncertainty around competition and AI funding despite strengthening hard disk drive (HDD) fundamentals.

Analysts led by Erik Woodring said the recent selloff has created an attractive buying opportunity, arguing that the market is pricing in an overly pessimistic end to the HDD upcycle. The firm said it would remain "aggressive buyers" of both stocks ahead of quarterly earnings.
Recent industry checks suggest accelerating storage demand, a widening customer base and a potential supply shortfall of roughly 400 exabytes in 2027 and 2028. Morgan Stanley also pointed to spot HDD transactions at prices two to five times contracted levels, suggesting further upside to margins and earnings.
Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »
The analysts said HDD manufacturers are at a similar stage of their cycle as memory chipmakers were a year ago, with pricing gains still accelerating and margins well below potential peaks. They argued that current valuations imply an "overly punitive cycle-end," including an 80% collapse in solid-state drive pricing over the coming years.
Morgan Stanley expects both companies to beat September-quarter expectations and deliver stronger-than-anticipated December-quarter guidance, with its earnings forecasts approximately 12% above consensus for Seagate and 10% above for Western Digital.
The firm maintained Overweight ratings on both companies and reinstated Seagate as its top pick in IT hardware, although it sees Western Digital offering the more attractive near-term earnings setup. The revised targets reflect lower valuation multiples amid concerns over industry competition and AI financing rather than deteriorating earnings expectations.
Western Digital shares have fallen roughly 21% over the past month, while Seagate has declined about 25%, amid a broader selloff in the sector driven by concerns over AI spending and the durability of the storage demand cycle.

Sentiment improved after JPMorgan upgraded Intel to neutral from underweight, while the 10-year Treasury yield retreated.Hardware suppliers sit directly exposed to hyperscaler infrastructure budgets.

Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) Rides AI Storage Demand, Is It Still Undervalued?
Seagate Technology Holdings (STX) is back in focus as investors track rising demand for memory and storage tied to AI workloads, along with its HAMR-based Mozaic platform for higher-capacity, power-efficient drives.
Recent trading has been strong for Seagate Technology Holdings, with a 1-day share price return of 1.20% and a 30-day share price gain of 10.49% helping offset a 90-day share price decline of 4.99% as investors reassess AI storage demand and risk. For anyone looking beyond the latest move to US$916.83, the stock shows notable momentum in the background. The year-to-date share price return is 218.85% and the 1-year total shareholder return is 303.74%. These contribute to a very large 3-year and 5-year total shareholder return that both exceed 10x.
Scan beyond Seagate Technology Holdings and see which storage and AI infrastructure peers are also attracting attention in the 85 AI infrastructure stocks.
Seagate Technology Holdings now sits on a huge AI storage story and a share price that has already moved sharply. The real tension is whether that momentum still lines up with a sensible valuation.
Most Popular Narrative: 20.9% Undervalued
On the narrative view, Seagate Technology Holdings is priced at $916.83 against an implied fair value of $1,158.73, which suggests the share price sits below where the story says it should be while also running far ahead of where it started this year.
Seagate is the storage-capacity position in a portfolio built on physical scarcity, and it''s the one I''d defend furthest into a downturn.
Not because the shortage is more durable than the others, it may or may not be. Because Seagate is the only one of my three storage holdings with a margin lever that runs independently of the pricing cycle.
See why 6 investors see Seagate Technology Holdings as 21% undervalued.
The most followed storyline, according to isidrohg, rests on two moving parts that both matter for valuation. The first is a tight nearline HDD market where supply has not seen new capacity in roughly a decade. The second is the HAMR driven Mozaic platform, which is described as pushing areal density higher so that each exabyte shipped requires fewer physical components, lowering unit costs even if pricing conditions change.
In that framework, Seagate Technology Holdings is treated less like a simple pricing beneficiary and more like a business with its own internal cost curve. The narrative points to HAMR penetration moving from roughly 40% of nearline exabyte shipments toward a targeted 70% by June 2027, and links that shift directly to higher gross margins that are tied to technology mix rather than solely to contract prices.
Supporters of this view also highlight how that cost lever interacts with capital allocation and balance sheet choices. The emphasis on using recent free cash flow to cut debt, rather than pouring money into new greenfield capacity, is framed as a way to keep the current HDD duopoly tight, which in turn underpins the cash flow assumptions that feed into the fair value estimate of $1,158.73.
Result: Fair Value of $1,158.73 (UNDERVALUED)
Still, Seagate Technology Holdings faces two clear pressure points: a potential HDD duopoly crack from new capacity and Western Digital closing the HAMR efficiency gap faster than expected.
Find out about the key risks to this Seagate Technology Holdings narrative.
Another View: What Seagate's P/E Is Telling Investors
The narrative and cash flow work suggest Seagate Technology Holdings trades roughly 21% below a fair value of $1,158.73. A simple P/E cross-check tells a very different story. At 65.5x earnings, the stock is far richer than both peers on 25.8x and the wider Tech group on 19.8x, and it also sits above an estimated fair ratio of 54.8x. That kind of gap points to real valuation risk if the growth story slips even modestly. The key question is which lens you trust more when the next wobble hits.

Lumentum has a problem most companies would trade their entire marketing budget for. Its optoelectronic components are fully spoken for through 2029, according to Bloomberg, as tech companies race to build AI data centers.
The update came on October 9, 2026. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) said its capacity for these parts is sold out through nearly 2029.
The products in question are mostly advanced indium phosphide (InP) devices, including EML chips and pump lasers. These are light-based components. They help move data at the speeds AI infrastructure now demands.
The details: demand keeps outrunning the factory
Most of the buying pressure is coming from hyperscalers and other tech firms. Their goal is ultra-fast data centers built for AI workloads, and those facilities need a lot of optical hardware.
CEO Michael Hurlston acknowledged that Lumentum is still struggling to keep up with customers, despite significant work to expand production.
The size of that gap is striking. For certain products, unmet demand is projected at approximately 70% in 2027 and roughly 30% into 2028.

The timeline is the other headline. In April 2026, Lumentum expected to be fully sold out through 2028. By October, that window had stretched to nearly 2029.
Background: the numbers behind the backlog
In fiscal Q4 2026, which ended in June 2026, Lumentum reported revenue of $1.01 billion. That figure was up 109% year over year. The company credited most of that growth to its components segment, the same business now facing the capacity crunch.
Then there is Nvidia. In March 2026, the chip giant invested $2 billion in Lumentum. That money was tied to multibillion-dollar purchase commitments for Lumentum’s lasers and optical components.
What this means for AI infrastructure and investors
The downside sits with everyone downstream. Companies that rely on Lumentum’s parts may run into shortages. A 70% shortfall on certain products in 2027 is not a rounding error for those buyers. It could force tough choices about which projects get built first and which ones wait.
For anyone tracking the AI buildout, a few signals are worth watching. One is whether Lumentum’s capacity additions start narrowing the unmet demand figures for 2027 and 2028. Another is whether the sold-out window keeps sliding further out. It moved from 2028 to nearly 2029 between April and October. A third is how Lumentum’s components revenue tracks in coming quarters. The 109% jump in fiscal Q4 2026 set a high bar. Sustaining growth will depend less on finding buyers and more on how fast the company can turn new production capacity into finished parts.

Lumentum (LITE) Can’t Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:33 AM CDT 3 min read
According to Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) CEO Michael Hurlston, the company is now almost sold out of components for 2029, as he said in a recent interview. Just six months ago, he said Lumentum was on track to sell out by 2028. The demand outlook is strong, but Lumentum's strong demand raises the question of how much growth is already priced in. Meanwhile, see our Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 to see the 5 companies that rank higher than LITE.
Lumentum Can’t Meet 70% of Demand for Some Products. Why That’s Bullish and Risky for the Stock
The underlying details paint a more limited picture. Lumentum cannot meet about 70% of demand for certain products through next year. For some other products, supply constraints will leave 30% of demand unmet through 2028.
According to Wedbush Securities' Matt Bryson, this creates a favorable backdrop for optical-input suppliers such as AXT and for foundry and silicon photonics companies, including Tower Semiconductor and GlobalFoundries. The challenge is not a lack of demand but limited capacity. LITE's growth will depend on how quickly it can expand production. Lumentum's challenge is turning strong demand into actual sales, but which other aggressive growth stocks do Wall Street analysts see as having room to run?
Is a 46x Multiple Fair?
Lumentum's forward P/E stands at 45.70x, roughly 22% above its five-year average of 37.51x. This indicates that investors are paying more than they have historically. That premium reflects expectations for rapid earnings growth. EPS is projected to grow 151.24% this fiscal year from a small base, followed by another 64.80% increase next year. Based on current estimates, the P/E could decline to roughly 28x on 2028 earnings and 21x on 2029 earnings. This means much of the earnings investors are paying for today is expected to arrive within one to three years. The company's near sold-out capacity lends more support to those projections.
The stock is not undervalued, but its premium could be reasonable if Lumentum adds capacity as planned. Demand is already there; production capacity is now the key factor limiting growth.
According to our database, the number of hedge funds holding Lumentum fell from 123 at the end of Q1 2026 to 111 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest reached 8.96% of float as of September 30, 2026.
While demand remains firm and Wedbush sees potential benefits for Lumentum's suppliers, investor positioning tells a more cautious story. As artificial intelligence (AI) pushes computing power and data transmission to new limits, investors are weighing different paths to growth. Is Arm Holdings (ARM -3.06%) or Lumentum Holdings (LITE -1.44%) the better choice today?
Arm creates the foundational blueprints for the world's most energy-efficient processors. Lumentum provides the optical components that allow data centers to communicate at lightning speeds. Both companies are central to the infrastructure of modern computing, but they operate with vastly different business models and financial profiles.
Arm designs and licenses central processing units (CPUs) and other systems used in everything from smartphones to high-performance data centers. Rather than manufacturing chips, the company earns revenue through licensing fees and royalties on every chip sold. This model enables high scalability and profit margins in the semiconductor industry.
In fiscal 2026 (ending in March), Arm's revenue reached $4.9 billion. This represents growth of nearly 23% compared to the prior year. Net income was roughly $698 million, though the net margin decreased slightly from roughly 16% in the previous year to about 14%.
As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, indicating the company has very little debt relative to its net equity. The current ratio is roughly 5.3x, suggesting a strong ability to meet short-term financial obligations.
Trailing-12-month (TTM) free cash flow was $1.5 billion through the June quarter, but note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 69% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Lumentum manufactures optical and photonic products essential to cloud data centers and telecommunications networks. In its latest fiscal year ended June 27, 2026, Lumentum revealed that Customer A accounted for approximately 26.6% of revenue while Customer B accounted for roughly 15%. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as the loss of either client would be significant.
For fiscal 2026, the company reported revenue of $3 billion, which was an increase of about 83% over the prior year. Despite this massive top-line growth, the company reported a net loss of approximately $6.9 billion, although its operating profit (earnings before interest and taxes) was $525 million. The $6.9 billion net loss was due to a $7.7 billion non-recurring loss on debt extinguishment.
According to its June 2026 balance sheet, the company has a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x. The current ratio is nearly 1.7x, indicating about $1.70 in short-term assets for every $1.00 of short-term debt.
TTM free cash flow for the period was roughly $300 million. However, stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
Arm faces intense competition from established rivals and open-source alternatives. If major tech companies decide to design their own architectures rather than paying licensing fees, the company could see its market share erode. Additionally, the business relies on continued growth in the mobile and data center markets, and any slowdown in hardware upgrades would impact its royalty income.
Lumentum is highly dependent on a small number of customers for a significant portion of its sales, and many relationships lack long-term volume commitments. The company is also subject to complex trade policies and export controls, specifically regarding operations in China. Competition from global firms such as IPG Photonics and Viavi Solutions exerts constant pressure on pricing and operating margins.
Lumentum appears to be the more value-oriented choice as it trades at a significant discount to its peer across both sales and future earnings estimates.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?
Arm is a great business that generates high margins from royalties and licensing fees. It would be a solid chip stock to own, but Lumentum offers better value right now.
Analysts expect Arm to grow earnings at a 25% annualized rate in the coming years. However, Lumentum is expected to deliver 132% annualized growth, as the business scales and expands margins. Relative to their forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, Arm looks expensive, trading at a forward P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 4.3x, while Lumentum trades at an attractive 0.29x.
Lumentum is benefiting from data centers shifting to optical connectivity for AI workloads. Revenue surged 109% year over year in the recent quarter, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of growth and signaling strong momentum that may not be fully reflected in the stock's valuation right now.
Arm is benefiting from the growing demand for CPUs, and its expertise in designing power-efficient chips could help it gain market share in the data center market.
Both companies are meeting demand at crucial chokepoints for AI, and they both face comparable risks. But it's difficult for me to pass up the huge discrepancy between each stock's PEG ratios. I would buy Lumentum since it's growing much faster than Arm and commands a much lower premium for future earnings growth.

Lumentum’s optoelectronic parts sold out through 2029 as AI demand outruns supply
The laser and optical component maker says hyperscaler demand has pushed its sell-out window out by roughly a year in just six months
Lumentum has a problem most companies would trade their entire marketing budget for. Its optoelectronic components are fully spoken for through 2029, according to Bloomberg, as tech companies race to build AI data centers.
The update came on October 9, 2026. Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE) said its capacity for these parts is sold out through nearly 2029.
The products in question are mostly advanced indium phosphide (InP) devices, including EML chips and pump lasers. These are light-based components. They help move data at the speeds AI infrastructure now demands.
The details: demand keeps outrunning the factory
Most of the buying pressure is coming from hyperscalers and other tech firms. Their goal is ultra-fast data centers built for AI workloads, and those facilities need a lot of optical hardware.
CEO Michael Hurlston acknowledged that Lumentum is still struggling to keep up with customers, despite significant work to expand production.
The size of that gap is striking. For certain products, unmet demand is projected at approximately 70% in 2027 and roughly 30% into 2028.

The timeline is the other headline. In April 2026, Lumentum expected to be fully sold out through 2028. By October, that window had stretched to nearly 2029.
Background: the numbers behind the backlog
In fiscal Q4 2026, which ended in June 2026, Lumentum reported revenue of $1.01 billion. That figure was up 109% year over year. The company credited most of that growth to its components segment, the same business now facing the capacity crunch.
Then there is Nvidia. In March 2026, the chip giant invested $2 billion in Lumentum. That money was tied to multibillion-dollar purchase commitments for Lumentum’s lasers and optical components.
What this means for AI infrastructure and investors
The downside sits with everyone downstream. Companies that rely on Lumentum’s parts may run into shortages. A 70% shortfall on certain products in 2027 is not a rounding error for those buyers. It could force tough choices about which projects get built first and which ones wait.
For anyone tracking the AI buildout, a few signals are worth watching. One is whether Lumentum’s capacity additions start narrowing the unmet demand figures for 2027 and 2028. Another is whether the sold-out window keeps sliding further out. It moved from 2028 to nearly 2029 between April and October. A third is how Lumentum’s components revenue tracks in coming quarters. The 109% jump in fiscal Q4 2026 set a high bar. Sustaining growth will depend less on finding buyers and more on how fast the company can turn new production capacity into finished parts.

The timeline is the other headline. In April 2026, Lumentum expected to be fully sold out through 2028. By October, that window had stretched to nearly 2029.
Background: the numbers behind the backlog
In fiscal Q4 2026, which ended in June 2026, Lumentum reported revenue of $1.01 billion. That figure was up 109% year over year. The company credited most of that growth to its components segment, the same business now facing the capacity crunch.
Then there is Nvidia. In March 2026, the chip giant invested $2 billion in Lumentum. That money was tied to multibillion-dollar purchase commitments for Lumentum’s lasers and optical components.
What this means for AI infrastructure and investors
The downside sits with everyone downstream. Companies that rely on Lumentum’s parts may run into shortages. A 70% shortfall on certain products in 2027 is not a rounding error for those buyers. It could force tough choices about which projects get built first and which ones wait.
For anyone tracking the AI buildout, a few signals are worth watching. One is whether Lumentum’s capacity additions start narrowing the unmet demand figures for 2027 and 2028. Another is whether the sold-out window keeps sliding further out. It moved from 2028 to nearly 2029 between April and October. A third is how Lumentum’s components revenue tracks in coming quarters. The 109% jump in fiscal Q4 2026 set a high bar. Sustaining growth will depend less on finding buyers and more on how fast the company can turn new production capacity into finished parts.

Lumentum (LITE) Can’t Meet Demand. Can Its Valuation Hold Up?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:33 AM CDT 3 min read
According to Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) CEO Michael Hurlston, the company is now almost sold out of components for 2029, as he said in a recent interview. Just six months ago, he said Lumentum was on track to sell out by 2028. The demand outlook is strong, but Lumentum's strong demand raises the question of how much growth is already priced in. Meanwhile, see our Top 10 Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Stocks to Buy in 2026 to see the 5 companies that rank higher than LITE.
Lumentum Can’t Meet 70% of Demand for Some Products. Why That’s Bullish and Risky for the Stock
The underlying details paint a more limited picture. Lumentum cannot meet about 70% of demand for certain products through next year. For some other products, supply constraints will leave 30% of demand unmet through 2028.
According to Wedbush Securities' Matt Bryson, this creates a favorable backdrop for optical-input suppliers such as AXT and for foundry and silicon photonics companies, including Tower Semiconductor and GlobalFoundries. The challenge is not a lack of demand but limited capacity. LITE's growth will depend on how quickly it can expand production. Lumentum's challenge is turning strong demand into actual sales, but which other aggressive growth stocks do Wall Street analysts see as having room to run?
Is a 46x Multiple Fair?
Lumentum's forward P/E stands at 45.70x, roughly 22% above its five-year average of 37.51x. This indicates that investors are paying more than they have historically. That premium reflects expectations for rapid earnings growth. EPS is projected to grow 151.24% this fiscal year from a small base, followed by another 64.80% increase next year. Based on current estimates, the P/E could decline to roughly 28x on 2028 earnings and 21x on 2029 earnings. This means much of the earnings investors are paying for today is expected to arrive within one to three years. The company's near sold-out capacity lends more support to those projections.
The stock is not undervalued, but its premium could be reasonable if Lumentum adds capacity as planned. Demand is already there; production capacity is now the key factor limiting growth.
According to our database, the number of hedge funds holding Lumentum fell from 123 at the end of Q1 2026 to 111 at the end of Q2 2026. Short interest reached 8.96% of float as of September 30, 2026.
While demand remains firm and Wedbush sees potential benefits for Lumentum's suppliers, investor positioning tells a more cautious story. The decline in hedge fund ownership and short interest approaching 9% suggest that some investors remain skeptical of the premium valuation. Whether Lumentum can build capacity quickly enough will determine if its premium valuation can hold.
While we acknowledge the potential of LITE as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Optics Stocks Rally Ahead of Earnings: Applied Optoelectronics Jumps 5%, Lumentum Adds 4%, Coherent Rises 2%
Optics stocks are surging ahead of a cluster of November earnings reports, and one CEO's claim that his company cannot meet most customer demand for years has traders wondering whether the AI optical bottleneck is bigger than the market has…
Published October 19, 2026, 1:05pm ET · 3 min read
This graphic illustrates the interconnectedness of advanced optical technology, like that developed by Lumentum, with significant market and investment growth. © Shutterstock
Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) stock jumped 5% to $79.01 on Monday as optics names advanced ahead of upcoming earnings reports. Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE | LITE Price Prediction) shares rose 4% to $856.18, while Coherent (NYSE:COHR) stock climbed 2% to $236.93. The group found support from anticipation surrounding results due in early November and continued interest in AI-driven optical demand.
The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (BATS:LYTE) advanced 2% to $20.20. Broader markets also moved higher, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) up 0.56% to $767.49. Applied Optoelectronics and Lumentum are scheduled to report earnings on November 5, and Coherent is set to report on November 4, keeping near-term focus on guidance and order trends.
Optics Names Advance on Earnings Anticipation
Applied Optoelectronics shares led the session’s gains among the three. The company supplies optical components used in data-center and communications applications that have benefited from rising bandwidth needs. Traders positioned ahead of the November 5 report, watching for updates on AI-related optical demand and capacity utilization.
Lumentum stock also posted a solid advance. CEO Michael Hurlston recently noted that Lumentum’s components are sold out through 2029 and that the company cannot meet roughly 70% of demand for some products through 2027 and 30% for others through 2028. Those comments have reinforced the view that optical connectivity remains a bottleneck in AI infrastructure buildouts.
Coherent Benefits From AI Networking Focus
Coherent stock rose more modestly. The company has launched its PhotonLink integrated optics platform designed for co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and chip-to-chip connectivity. Coherent already has more than 10 customer engagements in these areas, with initial PhotonLink revenue expected to ramp in the December quarter.
Coherent can benefit from existing high-speed optical transceiver demand even if broader co-packaged optics adoption takes longer than expected. One analyst recently reiterated a Buy rating with a $395 price target, pointing to opportunities in both current products and newer technologies. Valuation remains elevated relative to historical averages, leaving limited room for disappointment.
The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF’s gain reflected measured interest across the specialty group. Photonic integrated circuits are seeing rapid expansion tied to high-speed data transmission and energy-efficient optical technologies for AI data centers. Market forecasts point to strong compound annual growth rates through the end of the decade as cloud and hyperscale operators scale optical infrastructure.
Similarities among Applied Optoelectronics, Lumentum, and Coherent include exposure to AI networking demand and optical components for data centers. Differences appear in product focus and scale, with Lumentum highlighting multiyear sold-out conditions, Coherent emphasizing integrated platforms, and Applied Optoelectronics concentrating on specific optical modules. The broader chip sector has also shown signs of stabilizing after a recent soft stretch.
Upcoming earnings will provide the next major checkpoints for order visibility and margin trends across the three companies. Lumentum’s multiyear capacity constraints and Coherent’s PhotonLink ramp offer potential catalysts if demand remains robust. Applied Optoelectronics faces similar questions around AI optical adoption and competitive positioning.
Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest given the volatility typical of optics and photonics stocks. Stronger-than-expected guidance or further evidence of sold-out conditions could support the shares, while any signs of softer demand or elevated valuations may pressure the group after the recent run.
