Braze shares jumped 51% after Salesforce agreed to buy the company for $47.50 a share in cash, about $5.66 billion in enterprise value.
Braze now trades just under the offer price, so the market expects the deal to close, which leaves little upside for shareholders.
Braze shareholders and regulators still have to approve the deal, and it isn't expected to close until Salesforce's fiscal 2028.
Salesforce shares fell 3%, while Braze rival Klaviyo jumped 12%.
Braze (BRZE:NASDAQ) shares soared 51% today after Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) agreed to buy the company for $47.50 a share in cash, about $5.66 billion in enterprise value.
That's a 58% premium to Monday's close. (Not a bad way to wake up.)
Salesforce announced the deal at 8:00 a.m. ET, before the open. Braze's board approved it unanimously. Co-founders Bill Magnuson (Braze's CEO) and Jon Hyman, along with Battery Ventures' Neeraj Agrawal, have also agreed to vote their shares for it, according to a voting agreement Braze filed this morning.
Salesforce wants Braze's real-time engagement tools inside Marketing Cloud and Agentforce. Patrick Stokes, Salesforce's President of Applications and Marketing, made the pitch:
"Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. Bringing that capability together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction."
Salesforce is getting a business that's still growing fast. Braze's revenue more than doubled in three years, to $738 million in the year ended January 2026. Analysts expect it to pass $1.2 billion by the year ending January 2029…

Why Is Salesforce (CRM) Down 5.5% Since Last Earnings Report?
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Salesforce (CRM). Shares have lost about 5.5% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.
But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Salesforce due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Salesforce, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
Salesforce Q2 Earnings Beat on Investment Gains, Revenue View Raised
Salesforce reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $5.90 per share, up 102.7% year over year. The bottom line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 80.43%.
Revenues rose 10.8% year over year to $11.35 billion and topped the consensus mark by 0.25%. Growth reflected momentum in Slack, Agentforce and Informatica. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR reached nearly $3.9 billion, up more than 210% year over year.
CRM's Q2 Revenue Mix Shows Broad-Based Growth
Subscription and support revenues increased 11.7% year over year to $10.82 billion, including a $440 million contribution from Informatica. Professional services and other revenues declined 3.8% to $525 million.
Agentforce Apps generated $7.19 billion in subscription and support revenues, with constant-currency growth of 8%. Data 360, Headless Platform and Other contributed $3.62 billion and grew 20% in constant currency. Regionally, the Americas generated $7.4 billion, Europe $2.76 billion and Asia Pacific $1.17 billion, with constant-currency growth of 10%, 13% and 12%, respectively.
Current remaining performance obligation (cRPO) was $33.5 billion, up 14% year over year in constant currency. Total remaining performance obligation reached $66.3 billion, up 11%.
Salesforce's Agentic AI Usage Accelerates
Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5 billion, rising more than 240% year over year. Customers completed 3.2 billion Agentic Work Units in the quarter, up 97% sequentially, taking cumulative volume across Agentforce and Slack to 7.0 billion.
Slack posted its fastest quarterly net new annual order value growth since the acquisition, while Slackbot users increased more than 150% quarter over quarter. Bookings from Agentforce One Edition and Agentforce for Apps more than doubled sequentially. Management also noted that first-half net new annual order value growth significantly outpaced annual order value growth.
Data 360 ingested 104 trillion records in the quarter, up 355% year over year. Zero Copy ingestion reached 82 trillion records, up 731%, underscoring the rising usage of the company's data layer alongside its agentic products.
CRM's Profitability Reflects Investment Gains
Non-GAAP operating income increased 10.3% year over year to $3.87 billion. The non-GAAP operating margin was 34.1%, down 20 basis points, while the GAAP operating margin fell 230 basis points to 20.5%. Non-GAAP cost of revenues rose to 20% of revenues from 19%, while general and administrative expenses declined to 5% from 6%.
Net gains on strategic investments totaled $2.61 billion compared with $6 million a year earlier. These gains contributed $2.53 per share to second-quarter non-GAAP earnings, providing a substantial boost to the quarter's bottom-line performance.
Salesforce's Cash Flow and Capital Return
In the second quarter, operating cash flow jumped 71.5% year over year to $1.27 billion, while free cash flow increased 81.5% to $1.10 billion. In the first half of fiscal 2027, the company generated operating and free cash flows of $7.97 billion and $7.65 billion, respectively. Salesforce ended the second quarter with $8.31 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $3.09 billion in marketable securities.
The company returned $364 million through dividends during the quarter and continued executing its $25 billion accelerated share repurchase program. Through the first half of fiscal 2027, capital returns totaled $27.9 billion. The share count was down 141 million shares, or 15%, year over year.
Salesforce raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $46.10-$46.40 billion from $45.90-$46.20 billion. The $200 million increase, or $300 million in constant currency, reflects $100 million of organic growth and $200 million tied to the pending Contentful and Fin acquisitions, partly offset by a $100 million foreign-exchange headwind. Non-GAAP operating margin guidance remains at 34.3%.
Salesforce lifted its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings outlook to $16.67-$16.71 per share from $14.06-$14.12. It continues to expect operating cash flow and free cash flow growth of approximately 4%-5% year over year. Updated guidance incorporates the anticipated contributions from Contentful and Fin and is conditional upon the transactions closing.
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, CRM expects revenues of $11.42-$11.50 billion, implying 11%-12% year-over-year growth, and non-GAAP earnings of $3.42-$3.44 per share. The company expects cRPO growth of approximately 14% year over year and in constant currency.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?
Since the earnings release, investors have witnessed a upward trend in estimates revision.
Currently, Salesforce has a nice Growth Score of B, though it is lagging a bit on the Momentum Score front with a C. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock has a grade of B on the value side, putting it in the second quintile for this investment strategy.
Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of B. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.
Estimates have been broadly trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. Notably, Salesforce has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). We expect an in-line return from the stock in the next few months.

Salesforce (CRM) agreed to acquire customer engagement platform Braze (BRZE) in a deal worth $5.66 billion, as it looks to strengthen its business-to-consumer marketing solutions.
Shareholders of Braze's class A stock will receive $47.50 in cash per share, the companies said in a joint Tuesday statement.
Shares of Salesforce fell 0.8% in Tuesday trade, while Braze surged 51%. Salesforce is down 9.3% this year, while Braze is up 32%.
Salesforce expects Braze's real-time engagement and AI capabilities to complement its existing platforms, including Customer 360 and Agentforce. The customer relationship management platform expects the deal to advance its strategy for a more "complete" Customer 360 and strengthen the marketing cloud's cross-channel personalization.
Customer 360 is a suite of unified applications that connects customer data across sales, service, marketing, commerce, IT and operations into a single platform. Agentforce is Salesforce's AI-powered agent platform.
"Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale," Salesforce's president of applications and marketing, Patrick Stokes, said in a statement. "Bringing that capability together with Salesforce marketing cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction."
Salesforce has established a credible AI strategy that reduces the risk of the company becoming obsolete amid a transition toward agentic AI, BofA Securities said Monday.
The deal, which requires approval from Braze's shareholders and clearance from regulators, is expected to complete in Salesforce's fiscal 2028. Salesforce said it doesn't expect the transaction to impact its 2027 guidance.
"Salesforce's platform will help us innovate faster and together we'll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers," Braze Chief Executive Bill Magnuson.
The company has about 2,770 customers, including Canva (CVNA), Instacart (CART), Urban Outfitters (URBN) and PayPal (PYPL) subsidiary Venmo.
Last month, Braze said it expected adjusted earnings between $0.64 and $0.65 per share on a revenue range of $910 million to $913 million for fiscal 2027. In August, Salesforce lifted its full-year revenue outlook after delivering a fiscal second-quarter beat.
In June, Salesforce agreed to acquire customer-agent company Fin for $3.6 billion. Last year, the company completed the purchase of Informatica for about $8 billion.
In the broader industry, ServiceNow (NOW) completed its acquisition of Armis in April for roughly $7.75 billion. SAP (SAP) acquired Prior Labs in July. Late last year, Workday (WDAY) bought AI company Sana for about $1.1 billion.

BRZE Stock Gets Multiple Downgrades After $5.66B Salesforce Deal — Analysts See Shareholder Win, Potential Boost For Software Valuations
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 10:49 AM CDT 4 min read
Wells Fargo downgraded Braze to 'Equal Weight' from 'Overweight', but raised its price target to $47.50 from $45, citing a favorable deal outcome.
Stifel downgraded Braze to 'Hold' from 'Buy' while lifting its price target to $47.50 from $35.
Piper Sandler also downgraded Braze to 'Neutral' from 'Overweight' following Salesforce's agreement.
Braze Inc. (BRZE) received downgrades from multiple firms on Tuesday following Salesforce Inc.'s (CRM) agreement to acquire the customer engagement software company for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value.
BRZE stock surged more than 50%, hitting a 20-month high, even as Piper Sandler, Wells Fargo, Loop Capital and Stifel lowered their ratings following the announcement.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
Analysts See Shareholder Win, Broader Software Implications
In a note to investors cited by TheFly, Wells Fargo downgraded Braze to 'Equal Weight' from 'Overweight', but raised the price target to $47.50 from $45. According to The Fly, the brokerage said Braze investors would likely welcome the acquisition.
The firm viewed increased deal activity as positive for the broader software sector, potentially helping investors address questions about long-term valuations.
Stifel downgraded Braze to 'Hold' from 'Buy', while lifting its price target to $47.50 from $35. The firm described the approximately 58% acquisition premium as "a win for Braze shareholders," noting that the offer values the stock at its highest level since March 2024.
Piper Sandler analyst Billy Fitzsimmons also downgraded Braze to 'Neutral' from 'Overweight' following the acquisition agreement, per TheFly. Loop Capital analyst Yun Kim also downgraded Braze to 'Hold' from 'Buy', raising the price target to $47.50 from $40.
Meanwhile, Jefferies said the acquisition could "re-energize" Salesforce's Marketing and Commerce Cloud business and strengthen its competitiveness against Adobe (ADBE). The firm maintained a 'Buy' rating and $300 price target on Salesforce.
Evercore Flags Salesforce Deal Price, M&A Pace
Evercore ISI said the rationale behind Salesforce's acquisition of Braze makes sense, given the latter's fast-growing consumer engagement business, but warned that the timing and price were "likely to be a bit of a debate," according to The Fly.
The firm noted that the $47.50 per share offer represents a roughly 58% premium to Braze's previous closing price of $30.04, and approximately 80% above its 30-day average share price.
However, Evercore also warned that Salesforce's recent pace of acquisitions could concern value-focused investors, while identifying ServiceNow (NOW) as a potential beneficiary of investor fund flows. The firm maintained an 'Outperform' rating and $290 price target on Salesforce.
Braze's Growth Drew Analyst Support Before Deal
Before the acquisition announcement, several analysts had maintained positive ratings on Braze following its quarterly results and annual Forge conference.
Braze's U.S. revenue rose 27.2% year over year to $125.6 million in its fiscal second quarter (Q2), while international revenue increased 24.9% to $101.7 million, according to its Form 10-Q.
Following Forge, DA Davidson maintained a 'Buy' rating and $40 price target, citing customer and partner feedback about replacing incumbent marketing platforms, According to Investing.com, Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated 'Overweight' with a $38 target,
Citizens maintained 'Market Outperform' with a $35 target, pointing to encouraging customer spending plans. Raymond James had also maintained an 'Outperform' rating with a $33 target following Braze's September earnings report.
The transaction is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal 2028, subject to Braze shareholder approval and regulatory clearances. Salesforce (CRM) said it does not anticipate changes to its fiscal 2027 guidance and has not updated its long-term financial targets in connection with the acquisition.
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BRZE stock flipped to the 'bullish' zone from 'bearish' a day ago amid high message volume.

Salesforce Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Braze
SAN FRANCISCO & NEW YORK (OCTOBER 20, 2026) — Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the world’s #1 AI CRM, today announced it has
entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Braze (NASDAQ: BRZE), a leading customer engagement platform, for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value. Under the terms of the agreement, holders of Braze Class A common stock will
receive $47.50 in cash per share.
Braze helps marketers build deeper customer relationships by responding to customer behavior in real time, coordinating
personalized experiences across mobile apps, websites, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and more. Its cloud-native, event-streaming architecture is optimized for high-volume, real-time B2C engagement, continuously updating customer profiles and adapting
customer journeys while powering trillions of messages and journey actions each year. BrazeAI extends these capabilities with AI-powered optimization across content, offers, channels, and timing, helping
marketers make each interaction more relevant.
“Every interaction is an opportunity to wow your customers,” said Patrick Stokes, President,
Applications and Marketing, Salesforce. “Most of that wow comes from knowing your customer, and responding at just the right moment. Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale. Bringing that capability
together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM, and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction.”
the conviction that marketers and their creativity are a brand’s ultimate competitive advantage,” said Bill Magnuson, CEO and Co-Founder of Braze. “This past year we shipped at the fastest
pace in our history, and BrazeAI is helping marketers get their best ideas live faster. Salesforce shares our commitment to marketers, and we’ll continue building as Braze and investing in the Braze community of customers and partners who
built this company with us. Salesforce’s platform will help us innovate faster and together we’ll help marketers around the world build deeper, more lasting relationships with their customers.”
AI is raising the bar for marketers, who now need agentic solutions that can understand customers, make decisions, and act in real time. Salesforce is moving
to lead that shift, through both organic innovation and acquisitions that meet the standards of our M&A framework: advancing customer success, fitting within our strategy, accelerating innovation, and creating long-term value.
Following the close of the transaction, Braze’s real-time engagement and AI decisioning capabilities are expected to complement all four layers of
Salesforce’s architecture — Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and SIForce. Within Customer 360, Braze is expected to strengthen Marketing Cloud’s cross-channel personalization, helping brands turn a deeper view of each customer
into richer experiences, optimized in real time at the scale needed to reach hundreds of millions of people.
Salesforce’s vision for a more complete Customer 360 and expand how brands connect with customers across high-volume B2C experiences. Salesforce and Braze also share a commitment to an open, composable approach that gives customers flexibility
across the data, tools, and partners they rely on.
Together, Salesforce and Braze would help businesses:
Act on customer behavior in real time. Braze’s event-streaming architecture turns live customer
signals and data from cloud data warehouses and other platforms into personalized messages and coordinated journeys, helping marketers adapt engagement as customers browse, buy, and use products.
Deliver richer experiences across channels. Braze’s deep mobile and app capabilities, including in-app messages, personalized content feeds, and live updates, work alongside email, web, and messaging channels to create more connected customer experiences.
Make personalization more intelligent. Braze’s AI decisioning helps marketers optimize content,
offers, channels, and timing. Bringing these capabilities together with Salesforce’s customer context and Agentforce would help businesses make engagement more relevant and connect marketing with the broader customer relationship across
commerce, sales, and service.
Braze serves approximately 2,770 customers, including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban
Outfitters, and Venmo. Led by co-founders Bill Magnuson and Jon Hyman, Braze would also bring deep expertise in mobile experiences, data engineering, and customer engagement to Salesforce Marketing Cloud.
in Salesforce’s fiscal year 2028, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by Braze’s shareholders and receipt of required regulatory approvals. There is no anticipated change to Salesforce’s FY27 guidance.
Salesforce has not guided FY28 and there is no update to long-term targets at this time.

Burling LLP are serving as legal counsel to Salesforce.

NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Leading securities law firm Bleichmar Fonti & Auld LLP announces that a class action lawsuit has been filed against AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) and certain of the company's senior executives for securities fraud after significant stock drops resulting from potential violations of the federal securities laws.
If you invested in AppLovin, you are encouraged to obtain additional information by visiting: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/applovin-class-action-lawsuit.
Key Details of the AppLovin ($APP) Class Action:
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: November 16, 2026
Alleged Misconduct: Securities fraud alleging AppLovin misrepresented the strength, viability, and development of its AI-based business model and products
Largest Alleged Stock Drop: August 5, 2026 – 20% Stock Drop
Court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
Action: Contact BFA Law to discuss your rights
Investors have until November 16, 2026 to ask the Court to be appointed to lead the case. The complaint asserts securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of investors in AppLovin securities. The class action is pending in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. It is captioned Talbot v. AppLovin Corp., et al., No. 26-cv-10584.
Why is AppLovin Being Sued for Securities Fraud?
AppLovin is an advertising solutions company. AppLovin claims its advertising products use artificial intelligence ("AI") models, among other things, to more effectively match advertisers to prospective customers.
According to the complaint, AppLovin touted the purported strength of the company's AI models as a major driver of the company's growth, telling investors that AppLovin was "constantly improving" its models and that "we don't really see a reason why that's going to slow down."
As alleged, the company's new generative AI video tool in its AppLovin Ads platform experienced significant development delays, which stymied improvements to AppLovin's AI model.
Why did AppLovin's Stock Drop?
On July 13, 2026, a Bank of America Securities analyst published a note stating that "AppLovin's eCommerce footprint expanded at a slower pace in June" and "[w]eekly data has not shown a clear uptick since AppLovin [Ads] opened to all eComm advertisers on 6/22, suggesting a muted GA start." Accordingly, Bank of America Securities lowered its estimate for AppLovin's annual revenue.
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $64.13 per share, or 12.6%, from a closing price of $506.80 per share on July 10, 2026, to a closing price of $442.85 per share on July 13, 2026.
Then, on August 5, 2026, after the market closed, AppLovin announced that it missed consensus estimates for quarterly revenue, delivering $1.92 billion of revenue against consensus estimates of $1.94 billion. Defendants attributed the miss, in part, to delays in the roll out of AppLovin Ads' generative AI video creation tool, which led to lower-than-expected AppLovin Ads revenue and hampered AppLovin's AI "model performance[.]"
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $82.13 per share, or 19.6%, from a closing price of $417.80 per share on August 5, 2026, to a closing price of $335.67 per share on August 6, 2026.
Click here for more information: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/applovin-class-action-lawsuit.

Yet the stock is priced as if that pace is about to fade. At about 16 times forward earnings, AppLovin sits far below the multiple it has averaged over the past five years. The facts support a view that the discount is wider than the business justifies, though one weakness keeps that view from being a strong one.
AppLovin sells advertising software that works for the advertiser. Its AI-powered platform, called AppLovin Ads, helps businesses decide where to place their ads, and the company's quarterly filing says substantially all of its revenue comes from it. Free cash flow backs that up at $863.3 million for the quarter, and management put part of it into buying back the company's own shares. Sales are also spread across regions: U.S. revenue was $989.6 million in the quarter, and the rest of the world brought in $934.1 million.
Revenue grew about 30% a year over the past five years, so the latest quarter came on top of a long record. The same quarter a year earlier brought in $1,259 million, far below this year's. That margin move is too small to change the view. Concentration does cap it, because a stumble in one product has nothing to cushion it. A shareholder owns one very profitable engine, with the next one still unproven. A single research note is reopening the debate over how much real merchant traction sits behind AppLovin‘s (NASDAQ:APP | APP Price Prediction) e-commerce push. AppLovin stock is down 3% to $281.31 this morning. Meanwhile, shares of The Trade Desk (NASDAQ:TTD) are up 0.2% to $12.20, sitting out the selling that has hit AppLovin stock.
Magnite (NASDAQ:MGNI) shares are sliding 0.7% to $25.08, a far softer decline than the one in AppLovin stock. Taken together, those moves frame the drop in AppLovin stock as a repricing of one company’s growth story, with little evidence of a broad ad-tech selloff.
Wells Fargo Calls the Pixel Spike a False Start
The pressure traces to a note from Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) telling clients that a recent spike in merchant Pixel installs at AppLovin looks weaker than the raw count suggests. Investors asked about Pixel adds over the past two weeks. Wells Fargo found that raw installs did rise while the mix of new sites failed to improve. Most of the new sites, the firm determined, were Asia-Pacific storefronts built on Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) with little or no measurable web traffic.
On a traffic-weighted basis, Wells Fargo sees no meaningful pickup, pushing back on the idea that AppLovin’s e-commerce customer growth had suddenly accelerated. Calling the burst a false start, the firm stated that a real e-commerce turn at AppLovin still looks more like a story for next year. Wells Fargo kept an Equal Weight rating and a $325 price target on AppLovin stock.
Analysts treat new Pixel installs as a merchant testing count. The tally is one of the few public indicators for whether AppLovin’s web advertising push is landing real stores. That role explains why a note on install quality is weighing on AppLovin stock, where selling centers on a measurement question with Wells Fargo challenging what the install count means for AppLovin’s merchant growth.
In any case, AppLovin stock is down 58% year-to-date. That steep slide has made AppLovin shares highly sensitive to any read on the company’s web advertising push, and a single note on install quality was enough to add fresh pressure.
Notably, Trade Desk stock is barely changed and Magnite shares are only slightly lower, which points to an AppLovin-specific repricing.
Fresh Pixel data showing installs from storefronts with measurable traffic could answer the core objection in the Wells Fargo note on AppLovin. A traffic-weighted pickup would challenge the firm’s view that a real e-commerce turn at AppLovin belongs to next year. Any shift in the mix toward higher-traffic merchants could matter more for AppLovin than the raw install total.
Careful calibration of one’s holdings makes sense given AppLovin’s 58% decline year-to-date and a Wells Fargo timeline that places a real e-commerce turn next year. Patience may be the best attitude toward AppLovin stock while the market sorts out how much of the company’s web growth reflects real merchants.

The games industry moves quickly and while stories may come and go there are some that we just can't let go of…
So, to give those particularly thorny topics a further going over we've created a weekly digest where the members of the PocketGamer.biz team share their thoughts and go that little bit deeper on some of the more interesting things that have happened in mobile gaming in the past week.
Questioning that report on mobile games ‘infested’ with trackers and where your data gets sent
A questionable report released today by ProtonVPN carries with it bold claims that some of the biggest mobile games in the world are “infested” with trackers that send your data to China, Russia, Israel and ‘Five Eyes’.
I found the report a strange one, yet it's been reported by a couple media outlets as is so far.
FYI I'm sure you know, but Five Eyes is an intelligence-sharing alliance that consists of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, United Kingdom and United States.
The report says some of the “trackers” included in games can send “large amounts of highly personal data to countries hostile to privacy, with minimal transparency and no meaningful accountability”.
The report examined the 100 most downloaded mobile games in countries such as the US, UK and Germany. In the US, it found that of the (presumably estimated) downloads, 98% of them send data to ‘Five Eyes entities’(?), 95% to Israel, 81% to China, 71% to Russia and 70% to all of the countries it looked into.
So what does this actually mean in practice, though? The report used open-source platform Exodus Privacy to analyse Android apps and detect ad trackers.
This then details widely-used ad networks on mobile - some of them simply headquartered in the named countries. I looked at one top game to see exactly what kind of trackers the report alludes to.
These include AppLovin, AppsFlyer, Facebook Ads, Google AdMob, IronSource (wasn’t this shut down?), Tapjoy, Unity Ads and others. Hardly insidious.
These companies and networks, of course, are just par for the course on mobile and key networks for running ads and driving user acquisition campaigns.
The insinuation that simply from this, your personal - and identifiable - data is then shared with government agencies or is accessible by criminals for some nefarious purpose that will impact your life seems disingenuous.
Part of the report states how some apps actively collect users’ physical location - but takes no lengths to explain how this information is tracked to individual users by external parties or, importantly, that location sharing permissions are strictly opt-in for Google Play.
It’s worth noting that the report also includes a link trying to sell the company's ad blocker included in paid plans.
I think there are some practices that could shock people (like panel data), but just reeling off ad companies and stoking up political tensions is, as I’ve said, in my opinion disingenuous.
I asked ProtonVPN for comment and they sent the following statement:
“This report is about exposure of data, not about proven misuse. We're not claiming that any specific government has accessed data from these games, but we're showing that the most popular games in the world contain trackers that send data to companies with links to countries such as China and Russia. In China, for instance, National Intelligence Law requires organisations to support state intelligence work. In Russia, surveillance rules give security services broad access to data held by Russian companies.
“Some apps may have a valid reason for collecting location information, but when this is tied to extensive data sharing (e.g. the apps with large numbers of trackers), then there is the question of what else may be done with the data. Most naturally, this would most naturally be used to enhance the performance of ad targeting by sharing it with international ad networks (some of which are in locations that a user may not be comfortable with).
“Some apps are quite meticulous with specifying in their privacy policies which ad networks and external analytics providers that they are sharing data with. Others make broader, non-specific statements. And some have privacy policies that make no reference to the trackers that they have, and seem more like generic website privacy policies taken from a template library to satisfy the requirements of having a policy. Of course, few people take the time to read privacy policies, as well.”
Mark Pincus reveals Zynga nearly acquired Supercell for $400m in 2012
There’s something interesting about the “what if?” stories that occasionally come out of the games industry. We hear about acquisitions that never happened, or job moves that could have gone a different way. Countless huge deals must have come close to happening, then fell apart, and we’ll probably never know about them.
This is a particularly interesting one, with Zynga’s founder Mark Pincus claiming he had a handshake agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to acquire the developer for $400 million in 2012, only for Zynga’s board to reject the deal.
You can understand why. Zynga had already had a rough experience with the acquisition of OMGPOP, which had made a popular title with Draw Something. However, the game’s popularity quickly faded. The board apparently didn’t want Pincus making another acquisition before proving he could manage what he already had.
But the timing makes this one pretty painful in hindsight. Pincus says Zynga was already watching Supercell closely, with Hay Day and Clash of Clans taking off. Supercell would, of course, go on to become one of the biggest success stories in mobile games.
It does make you wonder how many other massive deals have come this close and never happened.
Mario Kart Tour shuts down after seven years on mobile
This is a strange one for me. Despite being a big Nintendo fan, I never actually played Mario Kart Tour, so I can’t claim its closure affects me personally. And yet, I have a very clear sense of nostalgia for this mobile racing game.
I had just started university when Mario Kart Tour released, and I vividly remember my first time seeing the game in-person was on a new housemate’s phone as I walked into the kitchen. It sparked a conversation, I watched some gameplay, shared some information from the handful of videos I’d seen from Nintendo YouTubers, and suddenly that new housemate was that little bit easier to talk to.
I saw a few people playing it around that time - not big Nintendo fans, not Switch owners, but young adults who were nostalgic for Mario Kart Wii and gave the game a try. As for how many stuck with it for the duration, who’s to know. But for those who did, it seems a shame there’s no Complete Edition like Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp got when that game shut down. It’s a reminder that most live service games will only live for so long.
AppLovin takes legal action against Unity over Ad Quality DSP
This week, Paige covered the news that AppLovin is taking legal action against Unity over data collected through the latter’s Ad Quality SDK.
If you've been following mobile ad tech, AppLovin and Unity ending up in court probably doesn't come as a huge shock.
According to the lawsuit, AppLovin asked a San Francisco court to stop Unity from collecting data through its Ad Quality tool. AppLovin says the tool picks up information about the ads AppLovin wins and that Unity might be using that data to train models that bid against it. Unity says the data comes from developers who agreed to share it and calls the lawsuit a dominant company trying to handle competition through the courts.
In mobile ads, data is the product, so I can see why AppLovin is worried. But suing a rival as competition heats up isn't a great look either. It's also hard to ignore the history here - not long ago, AppLovin tried to buy Unity outright.
What I keep coming back to when I think about this case is the developers in the middle. It's their games and their players, yet the fight over that data is happening without them.
Nothing's been decided yet, but I'm curious to see where this one lands!

To own AppLovin, you need to believe its AI ad engine can keep delivering strong results for advertisers while the firm broadens beyond gaming into consumer and mid market clients. The recent reset in growth expectations and margin guidance puts the spotlight on execution quality rather than long term ambition. In the near term, the main upside catalyst remains clear model improvements that support ad spend without inflating compute costs.
The biggest near term risk is that slowing revenue momentum, legal overhangs around AI disclosures and data access, and heavier privacy demands combine to pressure profitability. Q3 results in early November are an important check on whether the recent Ads Manager upgrade and model refresh are translating into healthier advertiser budgets and stable cash generation.
The opening of AppLovin's Ads Manager to public self serve access is the most relevant development for this reset. You now have a business that is trying to turn a historically high touch, gaming led engine into a broader, more automated platform that mid market and consumer advertisers can use directly. That decision makes the growth story less about a few large accounts and more about onboarding, retention and model accuracy at scale.
This expansion path also sharpens both the upside and the risk around AXON model upgrades. Better tooling and easier onboarding can support catalysts such as diversification into consumer, lead generation and connected TV through Wurl. At the same time, any misstep that increases compute, compliance or legal expense faster than new budgets arrive, especially with the stock already down more than 50% over the past year, would weigh heavily on how investors view execution quality.

The same group is baking in forecast revenue growth of 24.4% per year over the next three years and a forecast revenue level of about US$13.1b by that 2029 estimate year. In simple terms, the earnings change required is an increase of roughly US$4.1b, taking AppLovin from US$4.4b to US$8.5b on the timeline analysts are using.

Why is AppLovin Being Sued for Securities Fraud?
AppLovin is an advertising solutions company. AppLovin claims its advertising products use artificial intelligence ("AI") models, among other things, to more effectively match advertisers to prospective customers.
According to the complaint, AppLovin touted the purported strength of the company's AI models as a major driver of the company's growth, telling investors that AppLovin was "constantly improving" its models and that "we don't really see a reason why that's going to slow down."
As alleged, the company's new generative AI video tool in its AppLovin Ads platform experienced significant development delays, which stymied improvements to AppLovin's AI model.

On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $64.13 per share, or 12.6%, from a closing price of $506.80 per share on July 10, 2026, to a closing price of $442.85 per share on July 13, 2026.
Then, on August 5, 2026, after the market closed, AppLovin announced that it missed consensus estimates for quarterly revenue, delivering $1.92 billion of revenue against consensus estimates of $1.94 billion. Defendants attributed the miss, in part, to delays in the roll out of AppLovin Ads' generative AI video creation tool, which led to lower-than-expected AppLovin Ads revenue and hampered AppLovin's AI "model performance[.]"
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $82.13 per share, or 19.6%, from a closing price of $417.80 per share on August 5, 2026, to a closing price of $335.67 per share on August 6, 2026.

AppLovin Corporation (APP) Grew Revenue 53%. What Must Happen to Defend Its Valuation?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:32 AM CDT 5 min read
AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) reported second-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 53%, yet its stock fell sharply after missing revenue expectations and management's own execution standard. The tension is not whether the advertising platform is growing; it is whether machine-learning improvements can sustain the exceptional margins and earnings trajectory implied by its valuation. In early October, analysts began questioning competing ad platforms' progress and the reliability of new e-commerce adoption signals. This makes AppLovin's stock less a straightforward growth story than a test of how durable its targeting advantage really is.
Second-quarter revenue reached $1.92 billion against a $1.94 billion consensus estimate, while EPS of $3.76 matched expectations. Adjusted EBITDA increased 58% to $1.61 billion, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin above 80%. Management said its important advertising-model upgrade arrived just after the quarter closed. The problem was timing rather than a reported collapse in customer demand, according to management, but the distinction matters only if later results confirm it.
AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) ranks fourth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit, behind three companies with very different economics. The more interesting comparison is whether AppLovin's extraordinary operating profitability can survive a market in which rivals increasingly adopt similar AI tools.
Zeta Global (ZETA) Tumbles as AI Dreams Turn to Nightmares
Incremental Compute Spending Could Help or Hurt
The company's advertising auctions improve as its models become more effective at predicting which ads produce sales. When advertisers earn better returns, they may expand budgets, giving AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) more data and incremental revenue. The company guided Q3 revenue to $2.055 billion to $2.085 billion, up 46% to 48% year-over-year, alongside $1.71 billion to $1.74 billion of adjusted EBITDA and an approximately 83% margin. That guidance assumes model improvements already deployed, not hypothetical later releases.
Yet compute is not free. Management explained that higher training costs are being undertaken where incremental returns justify them. It said roughly ten cents of each incremental revenue dollar could be spent on compute. An 80%-plus adjusted EBITDA margin gives the company considerable room for investment, but also means small efficiency setbacks can have an outsized impact on investor assumptions about its operating leverage.
The expansion beyond games has its own measurement problem; how AppLovin is extending its AI platform into e-commerce advertising analyzes why a larger addressable market does not immediately translate into verified revenue. Competition is another pressure point. In October, a court declined AppLovin's request for interim relief concerning Unity's Ad Quality SDK, without ruling on the underlying allegations. Jefferies' survey of mobile-game ad buyers led it to raise estimates for Unity while lowering its 2027 AppLovin revenue forecast by 5% and EBITDA estimate by 7%.
The Discount Is Real, but So Is the Premium
The Seeking Alpha data places AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) at 20.16 times trailing GAAP earnings and 16.76 times forward GAAP earnings, with forward non-GAAP P/E of 15.81. That last measure sits roughly 46% below the company's five-year average of 29.17, but about 26% above the sector median of 12.52. Forward enterprise value to sales is 10.91, nearly six times the sector median of 1.88. Accordingly, a much lower earnings multiple relative to AppLovin's history does not mean the business is inexpensive on every basis.
The consensus expects EPS growth of 60.49% in 2026, 27.30% in 2027, and 24.88% in 2028. The estimated P/E correspondingly falls from 16.76 on 2026 earnings to 13.16 on 2027 earnings and 10.54 on 2028 earnings, assuming a constant stock price and forecast delivery. The steepest growth is front-loaded, so valuation depends heavily on the bridge from rapid model-led gains to a more sustainable rate.
Free cash flow reached $863 million in Q2. Management expects full-year free cash flow conversion to normalize near 75% of adjusted EBITDA after tax and interest timing effects. The company ended the period with $3.05 billion in cash and around $3.7 billion in debt and repurchased or withheld about $551 million of stock. These are meaningful financial supports, but do not settle the question of how much customer acquisition efficiency can improve from today's elevated level.
Institutional Conviction Faces a Near-Term Test
Q2 2026 hedge fund ownership declined to 88 from 91 funds, while short positions increased to 11.61 million shares on September 30 from 10.56 million a month earlier, equaling 3.99% of float. The positioning is not exceptionally bearish by itself, but the direction contrasts with continued strong revenue growth.
Price-target cuts further illustrate the gap between current profitability and confidence in its future trajectory. On October 12, Oppenheimer reduced its target to $490 from $560 while lowering its FY2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA forecasts; BofA maintained Neutral but reduced its target to $325 from $400 on October 9, arguing that a durable reacceleration would be needed to justify a premium to other advertising giants. Wedbush remained Outperform at $560 from $610 on October 14 but reset estimates to a more achievable baseline.
The immediate test is therefore not simply another 50% revenue-growth quarter. It is whether the Q3 model upgrade drives measurable ad spending, consumer-advertising diversification, and cash conversion without permanently higher compute intensity. A different Reddit screen asks which stocks investors expect to rise dramatically despite substantial uncertainty, underscoring the distinction between an exciting growth narrative and the earnings needed to support its price.

Yet earnings expectations have held up considerably better than the stock price, raising an important question: Has the market already priced in too much bad news?
What's Driving AppLovin Stock Lower?
AppLovin reported second-quarter revenue of $1.924 billion, up 53% year over year but slightly below analysts' expectations of $1.94 billion.
CEO Adam Foroughi acknowledged weaker-than-usual improvements in the company's AI-driven advertising models during the quarter.

That growth advantage matters, but investors are increasingly concerned about whether AppLovin can sustain its momentum.

The company continues to generate strong revenue growth, while its valuation has contracted significantly.
AppLovin expects third-quarter revenue between $2.055 billion and $2.085 billion, with adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.710 billion to $1.740 billion.

If AppLovin meets guidance and demonstrates renewed AI-model improvements, its discounted valuation could offer substantial long-term upside.
However, another disappointing quarter could trigger further earnings-estimate reductions and share-price pressure.

If you invested in AppLovin, you are encouraged to obtain additional information by visiting: https://www.bfalaw.com/cases/applovin-class-action-lawsuit.
Key Details of the AppLovin ($APP) Class Action:
Lead Plaintiff Deadline: November 16, 2026
Alleged Misconduct: Securities fraud alleging AppLovin misrepresented the strength, viability, and development of its AI-based business model and products
Largest Alleged Stock Drop: August 5, 2026 – 20% Stock Drop
Court: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California
Action: Contact BFA Law to discuss your rights
Investors have until November 16, 2026 to ask the Court to be appointed to lead the case. The complaint asserts securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 on behalf of investors in AppLovin securities. The class action is pending in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. It is captioned Talbot v. AppLovin Corp., et al., No. 26-cv-10584.
Why is AppLovin Being Sued for Securities Fraud?
AppLovin is an advertising solutions company. AppLovin claims its advertising products use artificial intelligence ("AI") models, among other things, to more effectively match advertisers to prospective customers.
According to the complaint, AppLovin touted the purported strength of the company's AI models as a major driver of the company's growth, telling investors that AppLovin was "constantly improving" its models and that "we don't really see a reason why that's going to slow down."
As alleged, the company's new generative AI video tool in its AppLovin Ads platform experienced significant development delays, which stymied improvements to AppLovin's AI model.
Why did AppLovin's Stock Drop?
On July 13, 2026, a Bank of America Securities analyst published a note stating that "AppLovin's eCommerce footprint expanded at a slower pace in June" and "[w]eekly data has not shown a clear uptick since AppLovin [Ads] opened to all eComm advertisers on 6/22, suggesting a muted GA start." Accordingly, Bank of America Securities lowered its estimate for AppLovin's annual revenue.
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $64.13 per share, or 12.6%, from a closing price of $506.80 per share on July 10, 2026, to a closing price of $442.85 per share on July 13, 2026.
Then, on August 5, 2026, after the market closed, AppLovin announced that it missed consensus estimates for quarterly revenue, delivering $1.92 billion of revenue against consensus estimates of $1.94 billion. Defendants attributed the miss, in part, to delays in the roll out of AppLovin Ads' generative AI video creation tool, which led to lower-than-expected AppLovin Ads revenue and hampered AppLovin's AI "model performance[.]"
On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $82.13 per share, or 19.6%, from a closing price of $417.80 per share on August 5, 2026, to a closing price of $335.67 per share on August 6, 2026.

Why AppLovin’s Discount May Be Unwarranted Ahead of Q3
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 9:18 PM CDT 4 min read
AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) reports third-quarter results in early November, and the question hanging over it is whether the company can keep growing this fast. In the second quarter, revenue rose 53% to $1,924 million, and net income grew even faster.
Yet the stock is priced as if that pace is about to fade. At about 16 times forward earnings, AppLovin sits far below the multiple it has averaged over the past five years. The facts support a view that the discount is wider than the business justifies, though one weakness keeps that view from being a strong one.
AppLovin sells advertising software that works for the advertiser. Its AI-powered platform, called AppLovin Ads, helps businesses decide where to place their ads, and the company's quarterly filing says substantially all of its revenue comes from it. That makes the platform both the engine of the story and its main risk. If you're interested in AI investing, we recently compiled a report on 10 Undervalued AI Stocks to Buy Now.
Over the past 12 months, AppLovin's operating margin was about 78%. In the second quarter, its adjusted EBITDA margin reached 84%. A margin that high usually means each added dollar of sales costs the company very little to earn, which is the clearest sign of an edge in the software itself.
Free cash flow backs that up at $863.3 million for the quarter, and management put part of it into buying back the company's own shares. Sales are also spread across regions: U.S. revenue was $989.6 million in the quarter, and the rest of the world brought in $934.1 million.
Revenue grew about 30% a year over the past five years, so the latest quarter came on top of a long record. The same quarter a year earlier brought in $1,259 million, far below this year's. For investors looking for profitable software names, our list of 10 Most Profitable Software Stocks to Buy Right Now is worth a look.
The fair objection is concentration, since the filing ties substantially all revenue to AppLovin Ads. It also names e-commerce as a new market the company hopes to win, which is a goal rather than a result so far.
Guidance also points to a small step down in margin, with management expecting an adjusted EBITDA margin of 83% in the third quarter, below the second quarter's level.
That margin move is too small to change the view. Concentration does cap it, because a stumble in one product has nothing to cushion it. A shareholder owns one very profitable engine, with the next one still unproven. Two things would settle the question: e-commerce turning from a stated goal into revenue the company reports, and margins holding near their current level as the platform grows. Investors who want more beaten-down names can see our ranking of 10 Stocks Investors Are Running Away From.
On adjusted earnings, the forward multiple of about 16 sits about 25% above its sector's median and about 45% below AppLovin's own five-year average. So the stock costs more than a typical company in its sector, but far less than investors have usually paid for it. On a stricter GAAP basis, the multiple would look somewhat higher.
That price assumes growth fades much faster than the latest quarter suggests. For a shareholder, it leaves room for some slowing before the numbers disappoint. If you're looking for cheaper growth names, check out 10 Undervalued Growth Stocks to Buy Now.
Early November's report will show whether last quarter's growth was a speed-up or a peak. AppLovin has earned the benefit of the doubt on profit, but it hasn't yet shown a second source of revenue. Revenue inside the guided range of $2,055 million to $2,085 million, with the margin near 83%, would make a deep discount to history harder to defend.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of APP as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than APP and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

AppLovin Falls 3% as Wells Fargo Calls Pixel Install Spike a False Start; Trade Desk Sits Out the Selloff, Magnite Dips
Wells Fargo just challenged the metric investors have been using to track AppLovin's e-commerce progress, and the stock is paying for it. Whether the firm's skepticism holds or gets overturned by better data could define where AppLovin heads from here.
Published October 1, 2026, 12:02pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Business professionals analyze data with a digital overlay of advertising concepts, illustrating the dynamic landscape of online ad spending that companies like Meta Platforms are navigating. © Summit Art Creations / Shutterstock.com
A single research note is reopening the debate over how much real merchant traction sits behind AppLovin‘s (NASDAQ:APP | APP Price Prediction) e-commerce push. AppLovin stock is down 3% to $281.31 this morning. Meanwhile, shares of The Trade Desk (NASDAQ:TTD) are up 0.2% to $12.20, sitting out the selling that has hit AppLovin stock.
Magnite (NASDAQ:MGNI) shares are sliding 0.7% to $25.08, a far softer decline than the one in AppLovin stock. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is also down 0.1% to $738.80, leaving large-cap technology close to flat. Taken together, those moves frame the drop in AppLovin stock as a repricing of one company’s growth story, with little evidence of a broad ad-tech selloff.
Wells Fargo Calls the Pixel Spike a False Start
The pressure traces to a note from Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) telling clients that a recent spike in merchant Pixel installs at AppLovin looks weaker than the raw count suggests. Investors asked about Pixel adds over the past two weeks. Wells Fargo found that raw installs did rise while the mix of new sites failed to improve. Most of the new sites, the firm determined, were Asia-Pacific storefronts built on Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) with little or no measurable web traffic.
On a traffic-weighted basis, Wells Fargo sees no meaningful pickup, pushing back on the idea that AppLovin’s e-commerce customer growth had suddenly accelerated. Calling the burst a false start, the firm stated that a real e-commerce turn at AppLovin still looks more like a story for next year. Wells Fargo kept an Equal Weight rating and a $325 price target on AppLovin stock.
Analysts treat new Pixel installs as a merchant testing count. The tally is one of the few public indicators for whether AppLovin’s web advertising push is landing real stores. That role explains why a note on install quality is weighing on AppLovin stock, where selling centers on a measurement question with Wells Fargo challenging what the install count means for AppLovin’s merchant growth.
In any case, AppLovin stock is down 58% year-to-date. That steep slide has made AppLovin shares highly sensitive to any read on the company’s web advertising push, and a single note on install quality was enough to add fresh pressure.
Notably, Trade Desk stock is barely changed and Magnite shares are only slightly lower, which points to an AppLovin-specific repricing.
Fresh Pixel data showing installs from storefronts with measurable traffic could answer the core objection in the Wells Fargo note on AppLovin. A traffic-weighted pickup would challenge the firm’s view that a real e-commerce turn at AppLovin belongs to next year. Any shift in the mix toward higher-traffic merchants could matter more for AppLovin than the raw install total.
Careful calibration of one’s holdings makes sense given AppLovin’s 58% decline year-to-date and a Wells Fargo timeline that places a real e-commerce turn next year. Patience may be the best attitude toward AppLovin stock while the market sorts out how much of the company’s web growth reflects real merchants.

Mobile tracker claims, the Supercell deal that never happened, Mario Kart Tour's closure and AppLovin vs Unity | Week in Views
The Pocketgamer.biz team pick their highlights from the headlines this week and deliver the stories behind the stories
Share:
The games industry moves quickly and while stories may come and go there are some that we just can't let go of…
So, to give those particularly thorny topics a further going over we've created a weekly digest where the members of the PocketGamer.biz team share their thoughts and go that little bit deeper on some of the more interesting things that have happened in mobile gaming in the past week.
Questioning that report on mobile games ‘infested’ with trackers and where your data gets sent
A questionable report released today by ProtonVPN carries with it bold claims that some of the biggest mobile games in the world are “infested” with trackers that send your data to China, Russia, Israel and ‘Five Eyes’.
I found the report a strange one, yet it's been reported by a couple media outlets as is so far.
FYI I'm sure you know, but Five Eyes is an intelligence-sharing alliance that consists of Australia, Canada, New Zealand, United Kingdom and United States.
The report says some of the “trackers” included in games can send “large amounts of highly personal data to countries hostile to privacy, with minimal transparency and no meaningful accountability”.
The report examined the 100 most downloaded mobile games in countries such as the US, UK and Germany. In the US, it found that of the (presumably estimated) downloads, 98% of them send data to ‘Five Eyes entities’(?), 95% to Israel, 81% to China, 71% to Russia and 70% to all of the countries it looked into.
So what does this actually mean in practice, though? The report used open-source platform Exodus Privacy to analyse Android apps and detect ad trackers.
This then details widely-used ad networks on mobile - some of them simply headquartered in the named countries. I looked at one top game to see exactly what kind of trackers the report alludes to.
These include AppLovin, AppsFlyer, Facebook Ads, Google AdMob, IronSource (wasn’t this shut down?), Tapjoy, Unity Ads and others. Hardly insidious.
These companies and networks, of course, are just par for the course on mobile and key networks for running ads and driving user acquisition campaigns.
The insinuation that simply from this, your personal - and identifiable - data is then shared with government agencies or is accessible by criminals for some nefarious purpose that will impact your life seems disingenuous.
Part of the report states how some apps actively collect users’ physical location - but takes no lengths to explain how this information is tracked to individual users by external parties or, importantly, that location sharing permissions are strictly opt-in for Google Play.
It’s worth noting that the report also includes a link trying to sell the company's ad blocker included in paid plans.
I think there are some practices that could shock people (like panel data), but just reeling off ad companies and stoking up political tensions is, as I’ve said, in my opinion disingenuous.
I asked ProtonVPN for comment and they sent the following statement:
“This report is about exposure of data, not about proven misuse. We're not claiming that any specific government has accessed data from these games, but we're showing that the most popular games in the world contain trackers that send data to companies with links to countries such as China and Russia. In China, for instance, National Intelligence Law requires organisations to support state intelligence work. In Russia, surveillance rules give security services broad access to data held by Russian companies.
“Some apps may have a valid reason for collecting location information, but when this is tied to extensive data sharing (e.g. the apps with large numbers of trackers), then there is the question of what else may be done with the data. Most naturally, this would most naturally be used to enhance the performance of ad targeting by sharing it with international ad networks (some of which are in locations that a user may not be comfortable with).
“Some apps are quite meticulous with specifying in their privacy policies which ad networks and external analytics providers that they are sharing data with. Others make broader, non-specific statements. And some have privacy policies that make no reference to the trackers that they have, and seem more like generic website privacy policies taken from a template library to satisfy the requirements of having a policy. Of course, few people take the time to read privacy policies, as well.”
Mark Pincus reveals Zynga nearly acquired Supercell for $400m in 2012
There’s something interesting about the “what if?” stories that occasionally come out of the games industry. We hear about acquisitions that never happened, or job moves that could have gone a different way. Countless huge deals must have come close to happening, then fell apart, and we’ll probably never know about them.
This is a particularly interesting one, with Zynga’s founder Mark Pincus claiming he had a handshake agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to acquire the developer for $400 million in 2012, only for Zynga’s board to reject the deal.
You can understand why. Zynga had already had a rough experience with the acquisition of OMGPOP, which had made a popular title with Draw Something. However, the game’s popularity quickly faded. The board apparently didn’t want Pincus making another acquisition before proving he could manage what he already had.
But the timing makes this one pretty painful in hindsight. Pincus says Zynga was already watching Supercell closely, with Hay Day and Clash of Clans taking off. Supercell would, of course, go on to become one of the biggest success stories in mobile games.
It does make you wonder how many other massive deals have come this close and never happened.
Mario Kart Tour shuts down after seven years on mobile
This is a strange one for me. Despite being a big Nintendo fan, I never actually played Mario Kart Tour, so I can’t claim its closure affects me personally. And yet, I have a very clear sense of nostalgia for this mobile racing game.
I had just started university when Mario Kart Tour released, and I vividly remember my first time seeing the game in-person was on a new housemate’s phone as I walked into the kitchen. It sparked a conversation, I watched some gameplay, shared some information from the handful of videos I’d seen from Nintendo YouTubers, and suddenly that new housemate was that little bit easier to talk to.
I saw a few people playing it around that time - not big Nintendo fans, not Switch owners, but young adults who were nostalgic for Mario Kart Wii and gave the game a try. As for how many stuck with it for the duration, who’s to know. But for those who did, it seems a shame there’s no Complete Edition like Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp got when that game shut down. It’s a reminder that most live service games will only live for so long.
AppLovin takes legal action against Unity over Ad Quality DSP
This week, Paige covered the news that AppLovin is taking legal action against Unity over data collected through the latter’s Ad Quality SDK.
If you've been following mobile ad tech, AppLovin and Unity ending up in court probably doesn't come as a huge shock.
According to the lawsuit, AppLovin asked a San Francisco court to stop Unity from collecting data through its Ad Quality tool. AppLovin says the tool picks up information about the ads AppLovin wins and that Unity might be using that data to train models that bid against it. Unity says the data comes from developers who agreed to share it and calls the lawsuit a dominant company trying to handle competition through the courts.
In mobile ads, data is the product, so I can see why AppLovin is worried. But suing a rival as competition heats up isn't a great look either. It's also hard to ignore the history here - not long ago, AppLovin tried to buy Unity outright.
What I keep coming back to when I think about this case is the developers in the middle. It's their games and their players, yet the fight over that data is happening without them.
Nothing's been decided yet, but I'm curious to see where this one lands!

The complaint alleges that, throughout the Class Period, Defendants made materially false and/or misleading statements, as well as failed to disclose material facts about the company's business, operations, and prospects. Specifically, Defendants misrepresented and/or failed to disclose that: (1) the generative AI video creative feature for the company's AppLovin Ads platform was subject to significant development delays, making its release on AppLovin's timeline unlikely; (2) AppLovin overstated the rate of its improvements to its AI models, in turn causing the benefits and reliability of its value proposition of its AI models to be unreliable; and (3) as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' statements about the company's business, operations, and prospects were materially false and misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis at all relevant times.
Why did AppLovin's Stock Drop?
On July 13, 2026, a Bank of America Securities analyst published a note stating that "AppLovin's eCommerce footprint expanded at a slower pace in June" and "[w]eekly data has not shown a clear uptick since AppLovin [Ads] opened to all eComm advertisers on 6/22, suggesting a muted GA start." Accordingly, Bank of America Securities lowered its estimate for AppLovin's annual revenue. On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $64.13 per share, or 12.6%, from a closing price of $506.80 per share on July 10, 2026, to close at $442.85 per share on July 13, 2026.
Then, on August 5, 2026, AppLovin reported its financial results for the quarter and revealed, among other things, revenue below consensus estimates. AppLovin attributed the poor results, in part, to delays in the roll out of AppLovin Ads' generative AI video creation tool, which led to lower-than-expected AppLovin Ads revenue and hampered AppLovin's AI "model performance[.]" On this news, AppLovin's stock price dropped $82.13 per share, or 19.6%, from a closing price of $417.80 per share on August 5, 2026, to close at $335.67 per share on August 6, 2026.

Unity Software Sinks 10% Despite Wedbush Target Hike on Vector Ad Platform; AppLovin Falls 3%, Trade Desk Slips
Wedbush just raised its price target on Unity Software and praised its Vector ad platform, yet the stock is sinking hard while rivals escape with minor bruises. Something beyond the numbers is spooking investors, and the answer cuts to the…
Published October 14, 2026, 1:57pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
An investor reacts to a plummeting stock chart, reflecting the market's descent into 'Extreme Fear' as key tech stocks sink. © Atichat Wattanasin Stone / Shutterstock.com
Unity Software (NYSE:U | U Price Prediction) stock is trading at $42.13, down 10% this afternoon. Wedbush raised its price target on Unity shares and described the company’s Vector advertising platform as gaining traction. That decline suggests the advertising cycle is weighing more heavily than the platform’s progress.
Meanwhile, AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) stock is at $263.65, down 3%, a softer pullback than the one in Unity Software stock. Additionally, shares of The Trade Desk (NASDAQ:TTD) are at $11.94, down 2%, a smaller slide than AppLovin’s. Those declines confirm pressure across ad-tech, with Unity Software stock at the heavy end.
For sector-level and broad-market gauges, the Fidelity MSCI Communication Services Index ETF (NYSEARCA:FCOM) is down 2%, and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 1%. Thus, the drop in Unity Software stock stands out. This is notable against that background, since it’s several times the size of the move across the rest of the digital advertising group.
Strong numbers back the price target raise. In Q2 2026, Unity Software’s revenue rose 23.9% year over year to $546.47 million, topping expectations. Its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.28 also beat estimates.
Grow Solutions, the segment that houses Vector inside the Unity Ads Network, expanded 35% to $389 million. Unity Software’s Q3 2026 outlook calls for strategic revenue of $540 million to $550 million. The company is targeting generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) profitability as soon as that quarter. Yet, Unity Software shares are sliding anyway, as cyclical ad-spending worries outweigh execution.
Unity Software runs two businesses: the game engine studios build on, and an advertising network that places and monetizes ads inside mobile games. Vector lives in the ad network, competing with AppLovin for advertising spend. Create Solutions, the engine side, grew just 2% in the second quarter, leaving most of the growth burden on Vector.
AppLovin brings far greater scale, with second-quarter revenue up 52.8% year over year to $1.92 billion. Year to date (YTD), AppLovin stock was down 61%, a much steeper slide than the 5% decline in Unity Software stock.
The Trade Desk operates as a demand-side bidding platform. So its business tracks broad advertising budgets across connected TV, mobile, display and other formats. Its second-quarter revenue rose just 3% year over year to $715.1 million, missing expectations. Down 69% YTD, Trade Desk stock now trades at a P/E ratio of 12x.
FCOM holds no AppLovin shares, making the Fidelity fund a broad gauge of advertising demand; its 2% decline doesn’t confirm selling in any single stock here. Trade Desk stock is a small position, at 0.5% of net assets.
The next test for Unity Software is whether Vector converts analyst enthusiasm into reported advertising revenue. A GAAP profit in the third quarter and the planned November payoff of the 2021 convertible notes would give the bull case steadier ground.
Unity has $2.36 billion in cash and an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) margin that expanded to 29% from 21% a year earlier. Its third-quarter guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $185 million to $190 million, pointing to further margin gains.
For Unity stock, the open question is whether Grow Solutions keeps expanding fast enough to back the bullish case. Keeping their positions smaller can help investors manage their risk until Vector’s revenue contribution is visible.

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ: APP) faces a securities class action seeking to represent investors who purchased or otherwise acquired AppLovin securities between February 12, 2026 and August 5, 2026.
The suit follows the publication of a concerning analyst report on July 13, 2026 and the company's August 5, 2026 Q2 2026 financial results, each of which drove the price of AppLovin shares sharply lower.
The developments have prompted national shareholders rights firm Hagens Berman to open an investigation into claims that AppLovin violated the securities laws and urge AppLovin investors who suffered substantial losses to submit your losses now.
Class Period: Feb. 12, 2026 – Aug. 5, 2026
AppLovin Corporation (APP) Securities Class Action:
AppLovin provides end-to-end AI-powered advertising solutions for businesses to reach, monetize, and grow their global audience.
To investors, "uplift" is possibly the most critical driver of the company's revenue growth. The company improves its AI model to increase uplift, better matching the exact right ad to the exact right user at the exact right millisecond. In turn, this uplifts advertisers' return on ad spend, increases their advertising budgets, and (for AppLovin) accelerates high-margin revenue.
The lawsuit is focused on the propriety of AppLovin's statements about model improvements and uplift.
Most recently, several weeks into AppLovin's Q2, during its May 6, 2026 Q1 2026 earnings call, management left investors with high expectations for uplift and revenue growth.
CEO Adam Foroughi said that the most important milestone investors should focus on was the company's "improving the underlying model." He emphasized that "[l]ast quarter earnings, I mentioned we just had one new model that had just created an uplift[]" and "[t]he one we had a couple of weeks ago was quite substantial." He also explained, "that's why I highlighted […] that we saw a big acceleration going exiting the quarter[,]" and "then, April Q2, bigger than any quarter that we had[.]"
Investors' expectations began to unravel on July 13, 2026, when a prominent analyst published a report highlighting a lack of immediate advertiser influx following the general availability launch of AppLovin's advertising tools. In response, the price of AppLovin shares tumbled $64.13 (-12.6%).
Then, on August 5, 2026, the company reported its Q2 2026 revenue that was below midpoint. In apparent contrast to the "big acceleration," management said "[o]ur pace of meaningful model improvement was lighter than normal during the quarter[]" and "we didn't get the same level of model uplift we've seen in recent quarters[.]" This news drove the price of AppLovin shares crashing another $82.13 (-19.6%).
Between the two drops, the company lost over $44 billion of its market capitalization.
"We're focused on when during Q2 AppLovin first knew that the uplift and revenue acceleration investors had come to expect wasn't happening," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation.
If you invested in AppLovin and have substantial losses, or have knowledge that will assist the firm's investigation, submit your losses now »

Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. AppLovin recently opened its Ads Manager platform to public self-serve access, while guiding for high adjusted EBITDA margins and acknowledging a slower revenue trajectory and an execution miss against earlier expectations.
The AI powered ad engine that drives almost all of AppLovin's sales is now both the growth lever and the primary operational risk, as management works to improve models without letting compute and legal costs erode profitability.
The focus now turns to how this earnings reset, particularly the downward estimate revisions, reshapes AppLovin's investment narrative and risk balance.
Scan beyond AppLovin and size up other AI driven advertisers by reviewing our hand picked 39 profitable AI stocks that aren't just burning cash that already convert complex tech into real profitability.
To own AppLovin, you need to believe its AI ad engine can keep delivering strong results for advertisers while the firm broadens beyond gaming into consumer and mid market clients. The recent reset in growth expectations and margin guidance puts the spotlight on execution quality rather than long term ambition. In the near term, the main upside catalyst remains clear model improvements that support ad spend without inflating compute costs.
The biggest near term risk is that slowing revenue momentum, legal overhangs around AI disclosures and data access, and heavier privacy demands combine to pressure profitability. Q3 results in early November are an important check on whether the recent Ads Manager upgrade and model refresh are translating into healthier advertiser budgets and stable cash generation.
The opening of AppLovin's Ads Manager to public self serve access is the most relevant development for this reset. You now have a business that is trying to turn a historically high touch, gaming led engine into a broader, more automated platform that mid market and consumer advertisers can use directly. That decision makes the growth story less about a few large accounts and more about onboarding, retention and model accuracy at scale.
This expansion path also sharpens both the upside and the risk around AXON model upgrades. Better tooling and easier onboarding can support catalysts such as diversification into consumer, lead generation and connected TV through Wurl. At the same time, any misstep that increases compute, compliance or legal expense faster than new budgets arrive, especially with the stock already down more than 50% over the past year, would weigh heavily on how investors view execution quality.
What The Current AppLovin Forecasts Assume
Analysts sketch a fairly specific picture of where AppLovin could land by the end of this decade. The current consensus points to earnings today of about US$4.4b and forecast consensus earnings of US$8.5b by 2029, which implies roughly a doubling of profit. The same group is baking in forecast revenue growth of 24.4% per year over the next three years and a forecast revenue level of about US$13.1b by that 2029 estimate year. In simple terms, the earnings change required is an increase of roughly US$4.1b, taking AppLovin from US$4.4b to US$8.5b on the timeline analysts are using.

Why is AppLovin Being Sued for Securities Fraud?

According to the complaint, AppLovin touted the purported strength of the company's AI models as a major driver of the company's growth, telling investors that AppLovin was "constantly improving" its models and that "we don't really see a reason why that's going to slow down."
